issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
Capture and retain the exact prepared container state in Finelog after all setup and agent dependency installation and before the first agent action. Include the inner agent environment after setup installs dependencies; an outer image digest or project `uv.lock` does not describe packages installed later inside a nested container. Finelog is the durable record; collection must happen at the Iris/Harbor runtime boundary that can inspect the environment.

In the identity-SFT campaign, Harbor ran `uv tool install mini-swe-agent==2.1.0 --with mcp==2.3.0` in an inner Docker container. The outer Harbor lock pinned LiteLLM 1.92.0, but did not constrain this separate environment. Historical `vendor/harbor/src/harbor/agents/installed/base.py::_exec` attached captured stdout/stderr as logging `extra` fields on the message `Command outputs captured`; `trial/trial.py::_init_logger` used a default file formatter that omitted those fields. Retained logs and trial archives therefore do not establish the installed inner LiteLLM version. This prevented attributing exposure to a reported compromised package; it is not proof of installation or exfiltration. Related: #10262 (dependency drift and missing agent output), #9816 (sandbox isolation).

Done when:

- Before task execution, a durable snapshot records immutable image identity, build/source provenance, runtime/container identity, setup commands and outcomes, and resolved dependency inventories for every agent environment prepared by that boundary. Preserve lockfiles where present, exact installed versions and available package artifact hashes/origins; explicitly record missing provenance.
- Capture both initial container state and the post-install state handed to agent execution, including OS packages, Python tool environments and other agent package managers. Record runtime mounts, privilege, network settings and environment variable names without credential values. Use immutable filesystem/layer identity plus a content manifest for setup-time changes so package lists alone are not represented as exact filesystem state.
- Finelog records link snapshots and installer stdout/stderr to cluster, job, task attempt, Harbor trial and timestamps. Large artifacts may live in durable object storage with checksums and queryable Finelog references; the record survives container deletion and retries do not overwrite it.
- Successful installer output is retained, not just a message saying it was captured. Retain completed setup commands, installer output and available partial state when setup fails. Redact credentials from every retained artifact, including output, lockfiles and provenance URLs. Describe mounts without copying mounted datasets or secrets; mark all exclusions so the record does not imply a fully reconstructable filesystem. Collection must not import newly installed packages to inspect them.
- Harbor does not begin agent task execution until snapshot persistence succeeds; failures have a visible setup error.
- An integration test installs a dependency differing from the outer lock, deletes the nested container, and reconstructs the actual version and container identity from retained evidence. Cover setup failure, capture failure, retry separation and secret redaction.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

Marin's pinned Harbor driver delegates trial preparation to Harbor, so the Iris task sees the outer process while `Trial._prepare()` creates and installs into the inner agent environment before `_run()`. The installed-agent helper truncates command output and attaches it to logging `extra`; the trial logger does not persist those fields, and neither boundary records the prepared container state. Finelog's `Table.write()` is buffered and may drop rows, so its `flush()` cannot enforce the requested pre-execution persistence gate. No open PR found for #10481 or this root cause.

**Relevant code**
- [`trial.py#L222-L229`](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/14777c013bee9d75821bc19dd2f35824bc9f3e96/src/harbor/trial/trial.py#L222-L229) — preparation before agent run
- [`base.py#L304-L369`](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/14777c013bee9d75821bc19dd2f35824bc9f3e96/src/harbor/agents/installed/base.py#L304-L369) — installer output capture
- [`base.py#L694-L823`](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/14777c013bee9d75821bc19dd2f35824bc9f3e96/src/harbor/environments/base.py#L694-L823) — environment contract lacks inspection
- [`log_client.py#L278-L330`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/finelog/src/finelog/client/log_client.py#L278-L330) — buffered write and flush
- [`stats_service.rs#L131-L163`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/finelog/rust/src/server/stats_service.rs#L131-L163) — acknowledged durable write

# Proposed Fix

## Design

Add a Harbor trial setup recorder at the boundary that owns the leaf agent environment. `Trial._prepare()` records an **initial** state immediately after environment start and a **prepared** state after healthcheck, uploads, and `agent.setup()`, before any agent task action. On setup failure it records completed commands, their output, and the available partial state before finalizing the trial. A snapshot failure raises a typed setup error, so `_run()` is never entered. Add an inspection contract to `BaseEnvironment`; implement it for Docker (Linux and Windows) and Daytona direct/DinD, including the inner `main` container in DinD. An environment that cannot supply the required identity and inventory fails setup visibly.

Each state record identifies the actual container/sandbox and immutable image or root filesystem digest, Harbor and build source revision, build inputs, timestamp, runtime mounts (paths and mode only), privilege/network settings, and environment variable **names**. Collect OS, `uv`/`pip`, Node, Cargo, and other agent package-manager inventories, including every Python tool environment, with installed versions, available artifact hashes/origins, and sanitized lockfiles. Inspect distribution metadata and package-manager output without importing installed packages. Pair the base filesystem/layer identity with a hashed manifest of setup-time changes in the writable layer. Exclude mounted datasets, secret paths, and other uninspected roots explicitly; never describe an excluded filesystem as reconstructable. Provider-specific inspection must report unavailable fields rather than substitute the outer image or lock.

Record environment build commands and all setup-phase `environment.exec` calls at their common boundary, including successful stdout/stderr, exit status, and timing. Redact before any Finelog, artifact, logger, `config.json`, or exception write: use known injected secret values and encoded forms, credential-bearing URL parts and auth fields, plus explicit secret-path exclusions. Keep raw output transient in memory; reject persistence if sanitization or inventory validation fails. This also requires replacing the installed-agent helper's truncated `extra`-only output path for setup commands.

Write immutable artifacts under `output_dir/harbor_evidence/<job>/<iris-attempt>/<trial>/<digest>`, with SHA-256 checksums. Keep this prefix outside trial directories: [Marin deletes unscored trial directories on retry](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/runner.py#L157-L169). Add queryable Finelog snapshot and setup-command rows keyed by cluster, Iris task ID/attempt, Harbor job/trial, phase, and capture timestamp; rows carry artifact URI, checksum, status, and exclusions. Upload and verify artifacts first, then use a synchronous Finelog write whose successful response means the row is durable. Do not use `Table.write()`/`flush()` for this gate: that API marks dropped rows processed. Give the Finelog namespace and artifact store matching forensic retention, and use unique attempt identities so retries never overwrite evidence. Marin passes the Iris/cluster identity into Harbor and advances its Harbor pin after the Harbor changes land.

## Delivery and tests

1. Add a strict acknowledged Finelog writer and the snapshot/command schemas, with a test that rejects dropped or failed writes.
2. Add Harbor provider inspection and setup recording, including sanitized build and installer output and partial failure records.
3. Wire the Marin driver identity and pin, then run a local Docker integration test: install an inner dependency at a version different from the outer lock, delete the container, and recover its exact version and container identity from Finelog plus checked artifacts. Cover setup failure, capture/write failure blocking execution, retry separation, and secrets in stdout, lockfiles, URLs, and existing trial artifacts. Exercise Daytona direct/DinD provider contracts in their dedicated integration environment.

## Open questions

- Can Daytona direct expose an immutable leaf filesystem/image identity and a complete writable-layer change list? If not, which provider capability must be added before enabling the gate there?
- What retention window should the new Finelog namespace and referenced artifacts share? The current issue specifies durability across deletion and retries but no time bound.

issues.title: [finelog] Record container state before Harbor task execution

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
Require explicit human authorization before an agent can submit a workload that enables `privileged: true` or effective `allowPrivilegeEscalation: true`. In the identity-SFT campaign, an agent requested Iris's privileged profile to run nested Docker. The profile generated both settings without a separate human approval tied to that launch. Ordinary authorization to run an experiment must not authorize elevated host permissions.

Provide an authenticated approval page showing the proposed launch and its requested privileges. A human explicitly approves and signs that request; the service issues a verifiable approval record and archives the reviewed request and decision. A website URL is a suggested interface, not sufficient authorization by itself. The approval must require a human-controlled authentication factor that agent credentials and an agent-controlled browser session cannot satisfy.

Done when:

- The controller rejects these launches without a valid approval for every caller, including humans and agents; do not rely on classifying a caller as an agent. Apply this across CLI, SDK, direct RPC, parent/child job and retry paths. Enforce the policy against the final effective workload specification, including init/helper containers and backend defaults. Cover omitted values or capabilities such as `SYS_ADMIN` that make privilege escalation effective; changing profile names must not bypass the gate. Ordinary workloads must explicitly disable escalation where supported; an omitted value that enables escalation requires approval.
- The page displays the cluster, image digest, source/config digest, entrypoint and arguments, privileges/capabilities, host mounts/namespaces, network scope, credential/service-account access, justification and requested duration. Keep secret values out of the page and archived record.
- Approval is cryptographically bound to that request, the approving human, permitted cluster and a bounded validity period. Specify the allowed job/attempt scope. Material changes require fresh approval; tokens cannot authorize unrelated jobs or unapproved child jobs. Retries are allowed only within the explicitly approved scope. Enforce the approved maximum runtime. Approval expiry or revocation blocks new starts and retries; document separately whether revocation stops an already-running job, and show that behavior on the approval page.
- Agents cannot self-approve using their existing tokens, inherited user sessions, task credentials, network-location trust or a client-side confirmation flag. Restrict direct backend credentials so an agent cannot bypass the controller by creating a privileged pod/container itself. Revoked, expired, tampered or missing approvals fail closed.
- Archive the reviewed specification, approver identity, timestamp, signed decision, expiry/revocation and resulting job/attempt IDs in durable audit storage; expose a stable record URL through Iris and Finelog. An agent must not be able to edit or delete its approval evidence. Record denied attempts without secrets.
- Tests exercise an authorized launch and rejection of absent, expired, replayed, altered and self-issued approvals, plus child-job, retry and direct-backend bypass paths.

Related: #9816 (sandbox isolation and controller access), #10481 (container-state provenance). This issue requests an approval gate; it does not approve any privileged launch.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

`LaunchJob` checks only the requested elevated profile, and skips that role check in null-auth mode and for received federation handoffs. The effective workload can differ: Docker makes every TPU task `--privileged`, Kubernetes leaves `allowPrivilegeEscalation` unset for the default profile and its staging/log sidecars, and the backend renders these settings after submission. A profile-name gate therefore cannot enforce the issue's policy.

**Relevant code**
- [`service.py#L1546-L1560`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/service.py#L1546-L1560) — profile-only authorization.
- [`docker.py#L251-L282`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/runtime/docker.py#L251-L282) — TPU forces privilege.
- [`tasks.py#L690-L721`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py#L690-L721) — Kubernetes security defaults.
- [`tasks.py#L521-L602`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py#L521-L602) — staging container lacks an explicit security context.
- [`tasks.py#L2652-L2697`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py#L2652-L2697) — final Pod assembled at dispatch.

# Proposed Fix

## Challenges

Approval must describe the workload that will actually run. Iris selects a backend after `LaunchJob`, and the backend adds image defaults, sidecars, mounts, service accounts, network settings, and security contexts. A mutable image tag or job name cannot be the approval identity. [#9816](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9816) also documents task access to controller admin through trusted network ranges; ordinary controller authentication cannot serve as human approval.

## Design

1. Define one canonical, secret-free launch envelope for each backend. Resolve every container image to an immutable digest and bind the source bundle/config digest, cluster and backend, entrypoint/arguments, resources, every container's effective security context and capabilities, host mounts/namespaces, network scope, credential/service-account *names*, justification, replica/retry limits, and total runtime limit. Render init containers and sidecars before evaluating privilege. Unknown or unsupported effective settings fail closed; unprivileged Kubernetes containers explicitly set `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`. A capability such as `SYS_ADMIN`, a host Docker socket, or an omitted escalation field that permits escalation is treated as elevated. The current Docker TPU `--privileged` behavior needs approval until device access is narrowed safely.
2. Add an Iris prepare-launch RPC that returns this envelope and digest, and an authenticated approval page that displays those exact fields plus the justification, expiry, retry scope, revocation behavior, and record URL. Require an enrolled, attested hardware security key with WebAuthn user presence and user verification for **each** decision; validate the challenge against the envelope digest and the authenticated approver's allowlist. A dashboard cookie, IAP session, agent token, task token, browser confirmation, or network location alone cannot approve. Keep the signing key in a separate approval service/KMS identity unavailable to Iris tasks; issue a signed record binding the digest, approver, permitted cluster, unique submission incarnation, bounded validity, maximum total runtime, and allowed attempts. A one-time challenge prevents decision replay.
3. Carry the approval ID and signed record in `LaunchJobRequest`, the stored job, and each `RunTaskRequest`. The controller re-renders and verifies the effective envelope at submission and immediately before each start or retry; the worker and Kubernetes creation boundary verify an attempt-bound launch authorization before starting a container. Pin an elevated job to an approved backend and cluster; a federated receiving controller verifies its own cluster in the record instead of trusting the parent's authorization. A child job needs its own approval. A replacement with the same job name has a new incarnation and cannot reuse the old record. Enforce one absolute job deadline across attempts. Expiry or revocation blocks future starts and retries; a running attempt continues only until its approved deadline. The page must state this explicitly.
4. Store the reviewed envelope, WebAuthn decision evidence, signed record, approver, timestamps, revocation, sanitized controller denials, and resulting job/attempt IDs in append-only audit storage controlled by the approval service. Iris and Finelog expose a stable read URL and query index; their ordinary logs are insufficient as the authoritative record. Redact secret values before display or storage, and restrict write/delete access so task and agent credentials cannot alter evidence. Denials retain only sanitized identifiers and reasons.
5. Remove backend bypass routes: task service accounts cannot create Pods or read controller credentials; only the controller identity can create task Pods, with admission policy rejecting elevated Pods lacking a valid attempt authorization. Worker RPC and Docker API access stay unavailable to tasks without an approved, isolated launch. Coordinate task credential and secret changes with [#10475](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10475), [#10474](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10474), and [#9816](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9816). No open PR found for this approval gate.

## Testing and rollout

Test the canonical envelope on both backends, including TPU defaults, init/log sidecars, omitted escalation, `SYS_ADMIN`, mutable image tags, and changed config. Exercise valid approval plus missing, expired, revoked, replayed, altered, self-issued, child, replacement, retry, federation, and direct backend attempts. Run a staging end-to-end check with real WebAuthn and Kubernetes/worker credentials, then deploy approval issuance and audit storage before enabling fail-closed enforcement. Inventory existing TPU jobs first: enforcing the current Docker behavior would require approval for every new TPU attempt.

## Costs / Risks

This adds a separate signer, durable audit store, and approval availability dependency. A signing or revocation-service outage must stop new elevated starts. The present TPU default would block ordinary TPU work unless it gains a narrower device mapping or operators approve each launch.

## Open Questions

- Who owns security-key enrollment and approver removal, and what maximum validity/runtime should policy allow?
- Can TPU device access avoid `--privileged` on each worker type? Until proven, the approval gate must cover those attempts.
- Which admission mechanism on each Kubernetes cluster can verify an attempt authorization before Pod creation, including direct API clients?

issues.title: [iris] Require signed human approval for privileged agent launches

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
Enforce a boundary between the trusted Harbor driver and containers executing agent code in Marin's vendored Harbor runtime. Agent containers must never receive host/cluster administrative authority or ambient credentials. Environment variables passed into them must be explicitly opted in. Any sensitive setting encountered at that boundary must produce a prominent, redacted command-line warning that reaches Finelog and can be read by operators and coding agents.

Marin's driver deliberately forwards `AWS_*` storage credentials to its Harbor subprocess for remote `jobs_dir` writes (`lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/driver_config.py::_driver_environment`). That is a trusted-driver requirement, not permission to forward those values into an agent container. This issue does not assert that this subprocess handoff alone proves a historical sandbox leak. Related #9816, #10481 and #10485 cover isolation, provenance and human approval.

Done when:

- Construct the agent environment from a documented minimal runtime baseline and explicit per-job/per-agent variable-name opt-ins. Only trusted submitter configuration can grant an opt-in; task files and installed-agent requests cannot authorize access to host values. Never copy the parent environment wholesale or use wildcard forwarding. Apply the policy after all config merges and provider defaults, at container creation and each exec/setup call. Distinguish image-defined defaults from forwarded host values and inspect effective settings before agent code starts.
- Reject infrastructure credentials and administrative access even if a caller adds them to the environment opt-in list: cluster/cloud storage keys, controller/admin tokens, host service-account credentials, privileged mode, effective privilege escalation, Docker/container-runtime sockets and host credential mounts. Explicit opt-ins do not override this prohibition. Require no-new-privileges, a documented minimal capability set, and no host PID/IPC namespaces or unrestricted host devices. Root inside an isolated container is distinct from host administrative authority and must not bypass these checks. Model access must use a trial-scoped proxy capability; provider master keys stay outside the agent environment. Warn about the capability without printing its value.
- Detect sensitive settings in environment values/names, command arguments, files/mounts and backend settings. Use declared secret metadata and known credential names/formats; do not represent pattern matching as proof that arbitrary content contains no secrets. Reject unsupported backends that cannot enforce the boundary or verify their effective configuration.
- Emit a flushed WARNING/ERROR to stderr before any sensitive handoff or rejected request. Include stable diagnostic code, variable/setting name, provenance, trial/job identity, allowed/blocked action and remediation, never secret values. Warn on explicitly permitted scoped model credentials as well as blocked infrastructure credentials. A warning does not authorize a forbidden handoff. Do not bury these details in debug logs or unformatted Python logging `extra` fields. Use a submission/request ID when no trial exists yet. Iris-task warnings must reach Finelog through stderr; local pre-submit rejections must also print locally and have a durable correlated audit event, with delivery failures made explicit.
- Trusted artifact upload and verification credentials remain in separate trusted processes and are inaccessible to agent code, including through shared mounts, inherited environments and provider metadata endpoints. Apply the rules to installed agents' setup commands as well as model-generated commands, across the shipped environment backends.
- Integration tests seed canary secrets in the parent, exercise config merges, env forwarding and exec paths, and verify they are absent from the agent environment and artifacts. Verify explicit nonsecret opt-ins work, forbidden credentials and privilege settings fail before agent execution, allowed scoped credentials warn, and a captured stderr warning is queryable in Finelog with no canary value exposed.

Human approval for an infrastructure launcher in #10485 must not implicitly authorize passing that launcher's authority into agent containers.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

Marin intentionally gives the trusted Harbor driver storage credentials for remote `jobs_dir` writes. The current vendored Harbor runtime then has several paths by which task configuration or an installed agent can resolve values from that driver's ambient environment and pass them to container setup or exec. These paths need a common admission policy; they do not establish that a historical trial leaked a credential.

**Relevant code**
- [`driver_config.py#L203-L206`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/driver_config.py#L203-L206) — trusted driver environment
- [`base.py#L209-L213`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/environments/base.py#L209-L213) — task environment resolution
- [`base.py#L231-L310`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/agents/installed/base.py#L231-L310) — installed-agent host lookups
- [`docker.py#L337-L379`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/environments/docker/docker.py#L337-L379) — Compose process environment
- [`modal.py#L342-L366`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/environments/modal.py#L342-L366) — Compose host interpolation

# Design

## Boundary

Add a typed agent environment policy to the trusted Marin runtime overlay and carry it into Harbor's trial creation. It names permitted host variables per job and agent, with provenance; task files, Compose references, installed-agent descriptors and model commands cannot add names. Construct the agent environment from documented runtime variables with fixed values (initially `PATH`, `HOME`, `TMPDIR`, `LANG`), explicitly opted-in values, and trial-scoped model proxy configuration. Keep image-defined defaults separate from forwarded host values, and inspect the effective environment before setup or other agent code runs. Replace installed agents' direct `os.environ` lookups with this policy's resolved map. An opt-in never admits infrastructure credentials or controller/admin tokens.

Apply one validation contract after all task, job, provider and image merges at creation and before every setup/exec call. Reject known secret names or formats in environment values, arguments and mounted files using declared secret metadata plus conservative name/format checks; describe pattern detection as incomplete. Reject cloud/storage keys, service-account credentials, controller credentials, runtime sockets and host credential mounts. Remove trusted verifier and artifact-upload credentials from agent-visible mounts and environments. Give model access only through the trial-scoped proxy capability, warn when it is granted, and keep provider master keys in trusted processes.

For Docker and DinD, validate the final Compose configuration and inspect the created container. Deny privileged mode, effective privilege escalation, host PID/IPC, unrestricted devices and sensitive mounts; require `no-new-privileges` and a documented minimal capability set. Root inside a container remains possible only when these checks hold. For Daytona, E2B, Modal and other shipped backends, verify equivalent effective settings and block metadata/host credential access; reject a backend if its provider API cannot enforce or verify them. Recheck at exec because setup commands can add environment values. Do not mark a backend supported until its effective configuration is verified.

Emit a flushed, redacted WARNING or ERROR on stderr before every allowed sensitive handoff or blocked request. Include a stable diagnostic code, setting name, provenance, trial/job or submission ID, action and remediation; exclude values, argument payloads and credential-bearing paths. Iris task stderr must be queryable in Finelog. Local pre-submit rejection must also create a durable Finelog audit event keyed by submission ID; if delivery fails, print an explicit local error and do not perform the handoff.

## Implementation and validation

[PR #10473](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10473) already narrows Docker Compose's inherited host environment and removes Modal's implicit `${VAR}` lookup; build on that change rather than repeating it. [PR #10474](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10474) changes trusted secret delivery and should be integrated before finalizing the credential-source rules. Then land the trusted policy and backend enforcement with real backend tests that seed canary credentials in the parent and exercise task merges, image defaults, container creation, installed-agent setup and per-command exec. Tests must show permitted nonsecret opt-ins, fail-before-execution privilege and credential rejection, redacted proxy warnings, no canary in agent artifacts, and a stderr warning retrieved from Finelog. Coordinate the pre-execution state record with [#10481](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10481); human approval under [#10485](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10485) grants no agent-container authority.

## Open questions

- Which shipped provider APIs expose enough effective container state to verify environment, privilege, mounts and metadata access? Backends without that evidence must fail closed.
- Which Finelog write path should persist a rejection before an Iris task exists, with a stable submission ID and explicit delivery failure?

issues.title: [harbor] Deny ambient privileges and require explicit agent env opt-ins

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
Run installed Harbor agents without public internet access during task execution. Permit only a scoped model gateway and explicitly declared task services. A broad local-network allowance is insufficient: local addresses can expose controllers, other jobs, storage and metadata services.

Done when:

- Separate dependency preparation from execution. Receive the task Dockerfile/build context or immutable image reference, prepare compatible pinned agent dependencies in an isolated build stage, and retain verified build and package provenance. Execution must not resolve or download packages at startup. This does not require one universal image for all tasks.
- Enforce default-deny egress on the processes running installed-agent code and their tool sandboxes, covering IPv4 and IPv6. Allow only the approved model gateway and declared task-service endpoints/ports. Define necessary DNS access explicitly and prevent it from becoming unrestricted external access.
- Block public internet, unrelated jobs, the Iris controller, production storage services, host/provider metadata endpoints and undeclared private or carrier-grade NAT addresses. A dedicated service provisioned for the task may be allowlisted, including a task-local database or object-store fixture; declaring it must not grant access to production services or credentials. Enforce this below the agent process; environment flags or agent instructions are insufficient. Redirects, proxy settings and DNS changes must not bypass the policy.
- The model gateway authenticates a narrowly scoped trial capability and cannot act as an arbitrary network proxy. Model-provider credentials stay outside the agent environment. A separate trusted collector uploads artifacts without giving the agent storage credentials.
- Tasks that genuinely need external access declare that requirement and use a separately approved, auditable exception policy. No silent fallback to unrestricted networking. Document the installed-agent startup behavior that is supported offline.
- Run representative tasks for every retained agent from the initial Pi, OpenCode and mini-SWE audit successfully with public internet blocked. Verify permitted model/task-service requests succeed and controlled attempts to reach public, private, metadata and undeclared endpoints fail. Confirm failed downloads or update checks produce actionable redacted logs and do not weaken the policy.

The companion launch-path issue owns the runnable Iris recipe; the companion security audit reviews the retained agents. Reuse #9816 and #10486 for isolation and credential boundaries, #10481 for build/runtime evidence, and #10485 for approval of elevated infrastructure privileges. Network exceptions require their own explicit approval scope.

Companion issues: #10487, #10488.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The current Iris sandbox profile withholds cluster credentials, but its only usable network choices are no egress and broad public IPv4 egress. Kubernetes permits DNS plus public destinations for the latter; it has no per-trial list of model and task services. Marin's trusted Harbor driver receives storage credentials, so installed-agent code needs a distinct trust and network boundary. This spans Iris networking, Harbor's runtime, and #10487, #10481, #10486 and #10488; the duplicate-work search found no open PR for #10489.

**Relevant code**
- [`sandbox.py#L59-L120`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/runtime/sandbox.py#L59-L120) — three egress modes; sandbox defaults to INTERNET.
- [`controller.py#L465-L493`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/controller.py#L465-L493) — DNS and public IPv4 allowance.
- [`tasks.py#L837-L860`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py#L837-L860) — pod isolation selected at dispatch.
- [`driver_config.py#L203-L208`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/driver_config.py#L203-L208) — trusted driver inherits storage credentials.

# Proposed Fix

## Design

1. Add a trusted, per-trial service-access contract at Harbor preflight and Iris submission: one model gateway identity and endpoint, plus explicit task-service identities, addresses and ports. The default is empty. Resolve service names in the trusted control plane, reject wildcards, broad CIDRs, controller/storage/metadata targets and undeclared destinations, and bind the validated policy to the job attempt. A task file or agent process cannot extend it. External-access tasks require a separate, reviewed exception record with destination, purpose and expiry; an unsupported policy fails before execution.
2. Move task image and agent dependency preparation to an isolated build phase. Accept a task Dockerfile/context or immutable image reference; resolve and pin the retained agent's complete dependencies there, retain artifact hashes and build provenance, and hand execution an immutable image digest. Do not run package managers or update checks at agent startup. Require the post-install, per-attempt evidence from #10481 before the first agent action. Keep build network permissions separate from execution permissions.
3. Run installed-agent code and its tool commands inside the same restricted execution boundary, separate from the trusted Harbor driver and uploader. Build on `CONTAINER_PROFILE_SANDBOX`: no host network, service-account token, controller token, cluster Secret, shared cache, runtime socket or privileged mount. Enforce default-deny ingress and egress for IPv4 and IPv6 below the agent process, with only the gateway and declared service addresses/ports admitted. Allow DNS only through a restricted resolver for declared names, or omit it for fixed endpoints. Add node-level enforcement for host and metadata traffic, and verify the actual CNI before enabling a backend: [Kubernetes NetworkPolicy](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/network-policies/) alone does not guarantee same-node isolation, and its IP-block behavior can vary around service address translation. If the backend cannot enforce the contract, reject the trial.
4. Give the agent a trial-scoped model capability accepted only for the selected model's inference API. The gateway must reject arbitrary URLs, CONNECT and forwarding to other services; provider keys remain in the trusted gateway. Put artifact collection in a separate trusted process and network namespace that reads only the trial's output, uploads with its own storage credentials, and cannot pass those credentials into the agent. Coordinate effective env and mount validation with #10486 and the runnable Iris recipe with #10487. #10488 determines which pinned agents may use the path.

## Validation and rollout

First test policy validation and generated pod/network manifests. Then use an isolated test cluster to prove permitted model calls and a declared local database/object-store fixture work, while public internet, controller, unrelated job, production storage, metadata, undeclared private/CGNAT, IPv6, alternate DNS, redirect and injected proxy probes fail from both agent and tool processes. Repeat after a failed setup and a retry; confirm redacted diagnostics and no silent fallback. Finally run representative coding and trace tasks for each agent retained by #10488 with public internet blocked, and publish the tested backend/CNI and offline startup contract in #10487. No production rollout until the live enforcement probes pass.

## Costs / risks

Per-trial policy and a restricted resolver/gateway add infrastructure and operational work. Standard NetworkPolicy can miss node-local traffic; a passing manifest test cannot establish isolation. Keep unsupported backends disabled until their enforcement is measured.

## Open questions

- Which Iris backend and cluster will #10487 certify first, and what node-level enforcement can it provide for pod-to-host traffic and IPv6?
- How should short-lived task-service addresses be bound to a trial without admitting other pods or services at the same IP/port?

issues.title: [harbor] Run installed agents with only explicitly approved service access

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
Establish which installed Harbor agents Marin intends to support, and security-audit their installers and runtime behavior at pinned versions. Start with Pi, OpenCode and mini-SWE, which the identity-SFT campaign used. Pinning the agent version alone did not pin its transitive dependencies, and the retained logs did not establish the exact installed inner environment.

Done when:

- Publish the retained-agent list, pinned agent and Harbor revisions, an owner for each audit, and an explicit supported/disabled/pending status. Do not silently treat every upstream installed agent as reviewed.
- Audit setup scripts, package resolution, download origins and integrity checks, install hooks and update mechanisms. Inspect the dependencies and subprocesses actually executed, including transitive dependencies and separate tool environments.
- Audit environment inheritance, credential handling, filesystem/mount access, shell execution, network requests, telemetry, model-provider configuration, logging/redaction, artifact handling and process cleanup. Distinguish agent-host privileges from tool-sandbox privileges.
- Record a per-agent finding table with evidence, severity, affected versions, mitigation, residual risk and validation. Missing evidence must remain explicit; absence of a log marker is not proof of safety. Use static inspection and isolated controlled tests, not execution of suspect packages with production credentials.
- Define release-blocking criteria. Disable agents with unresolved blocking findings; enabling a previously unreviewed agent requires the same review. Re-audit relevant changes to installers, dependencies, runtime permissions or upstream versions.
- Validate retained agents under the companion Iris launch recipe and restricted-network policy, including canary-secret isolation, blocked unauthorized network calls and useful redacted failure diagnostics. A passing functional task alone does not satisfy the audit.

Related: #10262 (dependency drift), #9816 (sandbox isolation), #10481 (prepared-state evidence), #10486 (agent environment and privilege boundary). This issue requests an audit; it does not assert a confirmed compromised installation or credential theft.

Companion issues: #10487, #10489.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

Marin pins Harbor `14777c013bee9d75821bc19dd2f35824bc9f3e96` for its isolated driver, but its preflight accepts any agent registered by that Harbor revision; it does not mark installed agents as reviewed. In the pinned Harbor source, Pi and OpenCode run an nvm installer and install npm packages during setup, while mini-SWE installs uv and a Python tool environment during setup. Each has a path that reads model credentials from the driver environment. These are audit targets, not evidence of a historical leak. [#10262](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10262) shows why an agent version alone is insufficient: a newer LiteLLM dependency broke mini-SWE after installation.

**Relevant code**
- [`trial_driver.py#L104-L116`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/trial_driver.py#L104-L116) — accepts Harbor's agent registry
- [`driver_config.py#L53-L65`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/driver_config.py#L53-L65) — trusted driver receives storage credentials
- [`pi.py#L37-L54`](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/14777c013bee9d75821bc19dd2f35824bc9f3e96/src/harbor/agents/installed/pi.py#L37-L54) — setup downloads and installs packages
- [`opencode.py#L183-L208`](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/14777c013bee9d75821bc19dd2f35824bc9f3e96/src/harbor/agents/installed/opencode.py#L183-L208) — setup downloads and installs packages
- [`mini_swe_agent.py#L373-L405`](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/14777c013bee9d75821bc19dd2f35824bc9f3e96/src/harbor/agents/installed/mini_swe_agent.py#L373-L405) — separate uv tool environment

# Supported-agent audit plan

The deliverable is a versioned audit ledger and a release gate for installed agents. Record Pi, OpenCode, and mini-SWE as **pending** until reviewed; their audit owners are currently **unassigned**. No other upstream installed agent becomes supported through Harbor's registry membership.

## Challenges

The outer Harbor lock does not describe packages installed later inside task containers. The retained logs discussed in [#10481](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10481) cannot establish the historical inner LiteLLM version, so the audit must record missing evidence instead of inferring a safe state. Agent-host and tool-sandbox access also need separate observations; a functional trial proves neither boundary.

## Design and order of work

1. Reconcile campaign configs and launch records with the current Harbor registry. For each candidate, name an audit owner and independent reviewer, pin the Marin and Harbor commits, agent package version, task image digest, installer source digest, and resolved dependency graph with origins and available hashes. Record unsupported and pending agents explicitly in `docs/harbor-agent-audit.md`. Mark any unavailable historical version or artifact as unknown.
2. Review each pinned installer and runtime, including fetched setup scripts, npm/Python install hooks and transitive packages, update paths, subprocesses, telemetry, model configuration, credentials, mounts, shell tools, network destinations, logging/redaction, artifacts, and cleanup. Use static inspection and isolated tests with canary credentials; do not run suspect packages with production credentials. Publish a per-agent finding table with evidence link, severity, affected versions, mitigation, residual risk, validation, and owner.
3. Add a Marin-owned approval manifest and enforce it at Harbor preflight and execution. Match installed agents by agent name, Harbor revision, exact agent version, and immutable prepared artifact/dependency digest; reject unlisted versions, import-path bypasses, and newly registered upstream installed agents. A disabled or pending entry fails before trial setup with an actionable reason. Changes to installer code, resolved dependencies, runtime permissions, or upstream revision invalidate approval until the affected review is repeated.
4. Validate each approved candidate using the [Iris launch recipe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10487) and [restricted-network policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10489). Retain the prepared-state evidence from [#10481](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10481); verify the [privilege and environment boundary](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10486) and [Iris sandbox isolation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9816) with canary-secret checks, denied public/private/metadata requests, permitted model calls, useful redacted failure logs, artifact retrieval, and process cleanup. A passing coding task alone is insufficient.

Block release for unresolved critical/high findings, unknown executable provenance, credential or host-authority exposure, unenforced egress, or failed redaction/isolation checks. Record medium findings with mitigation and an explicit residual-risk decision before approval; record lower-severity findings in the ledger. Keep affected agents disabled while a companion runtime control is incomplete.

## Costs and validation

Failing closed can interrupt existing agent evaluations until their exact configurations are approved. The minimum regression check is a preflight and runtime test that rejects an unlisted installed agent or changed revision, plus isolated end-to-end trials for each approved tuple and a negative test for each boundary above. Preserve setup output and prepared-state snapshots per attempt so a retry cannot erase the evidence.

## Open questions

- Who owns and independently reviews each of the three agent audits?
- Which identity-SFT launch records establish the exact agent versions and prepared environments? Historical entries without that evidence should remain unknown.
- Which tasks need an explicitly approved external-service exception under #10489?

issues.title: [harbor] Audit the installed agents retained in Marin's supported runtime

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
Provide one documented and tested path for running installed Harbor agents on Iris for trace generation and evaluation. The identity-SFT campaign used privileged Docker-in-Docker without first validating a safer supported route. Users should not need to discover backend, networking and credential boundaries by trial and error.

Done when:

- Target Pi, OpenCode and mini-SWE. A checked-in launch recipe runs every agent retained by the security audit through the Marin Harbor runtime on Iris, with pinned versions and isolated task workspaces, without privileged Docker-in-Docker or host administrative access.
- Document where the Harbor driver, installed agent, tool commands, model gateway, build process and artifact uploader run. Identify which process holds each credential and how agent requests reach the model without access to the Iris controller or other jobs.
- The recipe accepts task Dockerfiles/build contexts or prebuilt image references, prepares dependencies before execution, and uses the restricted-service network policy tracked by the companion issue. Document supported task features and reject unsupported features before starting a trial.
- Artifact collection, per-attempt logs, dependency/container provenance, timeouts, cancellation, sandbox cleanup and infrastructure retries work through the supported path. Retries preserve prior evidence.
- End-to-end checks run a representative coding repair and an identity/tool trace through each retained agent. An agent excluded because of a blocking audit finding must be explicitly disabled and listed as unsupported; it must not be silently skipped. Verify model calls, actual tool execution, grading or trace capture, artifact retrieval and cleanup. Verify no ambient infrastructure credentials or elevated host privileges reach agent code.
- Publish a runnable example with prerequisite checks and actionable errors for missing runtime support, image incompatibility and unreachable model gateways. Declare the tested Iris backend/cluster requirements; do not imply untested configurations are supported.

Coordinate with the companion installed-agent security audit and restricted-network execution issues. Reuse #9816, #10481, #10485 and #10486 for isolation, provenance, privilege approval and environment forwarding controls. This issue owns the complete supported launch recipe and its end-to-end validation.

Companion issues: #10488, #10489.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

The shared evaluation launcher validates one-agent, one-dataset Harbor policies and runs a pinned driver, but its checked-in OpenCode policy uses Daytona. The driver holds object-store credentials; current Iris Kubernetes tasks merge cluster and job environment into the task container and can select a privileged profile. An Iris environment switch alone cannot meet this issue's isolation requirements. [PR #10392](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10392) develops Pi trace capture for SkyRL but does not provide the installed-agent Iris launch path; no open PR references #10487.

**Relevant code**
- [`trial_driver.py#L104-L127`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/trial_driver.py#L104-L127) — agent and environment preflight hooks
- [`driver_config.py#L147-L151`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/driver_config.py#L147-L151) — trusted driver environment
- [`grug-opencode-id.yaml#L20-L49`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/experiments/evaluation/configs/harbor/grug-opencode-id.yaml#L20-L49) — current Daytona OpenCode policy
- [`tasks.py#L783-L795`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py#L783-L795) — Iris task environment merge
- [`tasks.py#L690-L721`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py#L690-L721) — task privilege profiles

# Supported Iris launch path

Run the trusted Harbor driver in an Iris evaluation job and place each installed-agent trial in its own isolated Iris task. Keep image preparation, model serving and artifact upload outside the agent task. First qualify `cw-us-east-02a` only after verifying that its network plugin enforces the required policy; document that exact tested backend and cluster.

## Challenges

The current checkout has no Iris sandbox profile, and `cw-us-east-02a` sets `host_network: true` for ordinary tasks. The new profile must override that setting and remove inherited credentials before a trial can run. The supported agent list and dependency pins depend on the audit in #10488.

## Design

1. Add an Iris environment adapter through Harbor's existing `environment.import_path` hook and checked-in policies for Pi, OpenCode and mini-SWE. Reuse `experiments.evaluation.cli launch --harbor-config` and its effective-config preflight. The adapter accepts only agents marked supported by [#10488](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10488), with pinned Harbor, agent and transitive dependency revisions. List agents with blocking audit findings as disabled with the reason; fail before submission if selected.
2. Prepare each task in a separate trusted, unprivileged build stage. Accept a task Dockerfile plus context or an immutable image reference, add the audited agent dependencies, and produce an image digest and resolved package/build record for [#10481](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10481). No package resolution or installer runs after the trial starts. Preflight rejects unsupported architectures and runtime hooks, undeclared task services, host mounts, nested Docker, elevated privileges and unrestricted-network requirements before creating a trial; document the accepted feature set with each recipe. An unsupported build construct is an error, not a reason to change the execution privilege.
3. Launch one [#9816](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9816) sandbox task per attempt, with a private workspace and a separately prepared verifier environment. The trusted driver owns Iris submission and job credentials. Agent and tool processes receive only explicit nonsecret environment opt-ins and a trial-scoped model capability under [#10486](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10486); they receive no controller address/token, object-store credentials, host mounts, service-account token or Docker socket. Reject any privileged/effective-escalation request; [#10485](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10485) governs such launches elsewhere and does not make this recipe privileged.
4. Enforce [#10489](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10489) below the agent process: default-deny IPv4/IPv6 egress, with only the fixed model gateway and declared task-service endpoints/ports allowed. The gateway authenticates the trial capability and cannot proxy arbitrary destinations. After agent execution, a trusted collector retrieves the workspace and uploads redacted logs, trajectory, grading output and artifacts under attempt-unique keys. Persist the prepared-state snapshot before the first action. Timeouts/cancellation stop the task, cleanup follows collection, and an infrastructure retry creates a new attempt without replacing earlier evidence.

| Process | Location | Credential boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Harbor driver / collector | Trusted Iris evaluation task | Iris submission and artifact-storage credentials |
| Image builder | Separate trusted build job | Registry push credential; no model or evaluation storage credential |
| Installed agent and tools | Per-attempt sandbox task | Trial-scoped model capability and declared task-service access only |
| Model gateway | Trusted serving plane | Provider credential; fixed upstream and trial authorization |
| Verifier | Separate sandbox task | Task-local grading inputs; no model or infrastructure credential |

## Testing and publication

Add preflight tests for supported and rejected task features, disabled agents, missing cluster support, image incompatibility and unreachable gateways. On the qualified cluster, run a coding repair and an identity/tool trace through every retained agent; verify model calls, real tool execution, grading/trace capture, artifact retrieval and cleanup. Probe public, controller, metadata, other-job and undeclared-service egress; confirm the parent canary credentials and elevated privileges are absent from agent and tool processes. Exercise build/setup failure, timeout, cancellation and infrastructure retry with retained prior-attempt evidence. Publish the exact cluster/runtime prerequisites, pinned recipes, runnable command and actionable errors in `experiments/evaluation/README.md`.

## Costs / risks

The build stage adds registry and image-cache cost; per-attempt Iris tasks add startup latency. Network isolation must be demonstrated on the target cluster rather than inferred from a manifest.

## Open questions

The launch remains unsupported until #9816, #10486, #10489, #10481 and the retained-agent findings from #10488 have enforceable implementations and the cluster tests pass. Confirm `cw-us-east-02a` network-policy enforcement and an unprivileged builder that handles the task Dockerfile subset before choosing that cluster as supported. The audit must decide which of Pi, OpenCode and mini-SWE remain enabled. No live validation was performed during this triage.

## Overview

This document is an attempt to formalize Marin’s policy towards what constitutes reportable, public-facing, canonical eval results for Marin models as well as the baselines we compare against.

Why do we need this document? With the first “snowball” release of a 67B A2B MoE, Marin is entering a regime where we regularly compare Marin models to existing open and closed-source models. Because Marin’s unique claim is that we are open development, we will need to hold ourselves to a high standard of transparency on how we report eval scores of Marin models and what claims we make about Marin model capabilities based on those scores.

What is in scope? This document is intended to act as a living snapshot, trustworthy for any given period in time, as to the what and the how of Marin’s canonical set of evals, a set of standards to which we will aspire to hold ourselves. By "the what", we mean “which evals did we run, with what consistent set of hyperparameters and experimental constraints”. By "the how", we mean “where is the self-contained codebase that is both necessary and sufficient to reproduce our eval results independently”.

## Previous version notes

* Released Sept 24, 2026: 18 non-agentic benchmarks, 8 Harbor agentic benchmarks, and 4 reserved out-of-distribution benchmarks.

### In Distribution but Not Currently Evaluated (by contamination)
