issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
## STATUS
Sorry guys this is currently all AI-generated. Will clean up as we get further in the experiment.

## TL;DR

Design stage, 2026-10-16. We compare five supervised fine-tuning (SFT) mechanisms for agentic coding on one base, one task pool, one teacher and one supervised-token budget: plain SFT (one accepted demonstration per task), rejection-sampled SFT with resampling across epochs, relay SFT (#10027), recovery SFT, and plateau dropping (#10028). The earlier transfer experiments (#9920, #9984) compared plain SFT, rejection-sampled SFT, on-policy distillation and weight merging on non-agentic tasks; this experiment moves to agentic tasks under the eval policy (#10197) and drops merging and distillation. Nothing has trained yet except a learning-rate sweep of the control, which is in progress.

## Question

Which mechanism, if any, improves Snowball v0 on SWE-bench Verified and the terminal benchmarks over plain SFT at equal supervised tokens, without losing retention on GSM8K, BFCL-Parity and GPQA-Diamond.

## Fixed choices

- Base: Snowball v0 = `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Merge-Campaign3-DARE-Linear-02-2026.10.12` @ `4eeb756b`. v0 carries a diluted DARE graft of the allkimi relay SFT, so relay's lift reads smaller than it would on a pre-graft checkpoint; this is accepted because the question is what improves the release.
- Task pool: about 2,200 TMax environments (`allenai/TMax-SFT-16.5K`, tasks.zip) and about 2,100 SWE-smith tasks sampled from the Harbor packages in `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s`, stratified by repository, SWE-bench Verified repositories removed, decontaminated through DataKit against SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and TBLite 2.0. Selection is outcome-blind. SWE-smith packages receive a git-history strip before the agent phase (#10212).
- Harness per task family, matching the policy's scoring agent: TMax under Terminus-2, SWE-smith under mini-swe-agent 2.1.0, both in Harbor under the policy pins.
- Teacher: GLM 5.3 through the internal inference service, 8 attempts per task, verified by each task's tests. v0 is never sampled except in relay, where it starts each task and GLM continues after a trigger (format error, context budget, completion claim).
- Recipe, shared by every arm: the #9984 comparison-arm settings (AdamW, betas 0.9/0.999, weight decay 0, clip 1.0, router bias frozen, batch 16 at 32k context, constant learning rate, loss averaged over supervised tokens), 3 epochs, replay of general SFT data (`nemotron_sft_v3`, reasoning kept) at one quarter of the agentic budget. The learning rate comes from the sweep below.

## Arms and token matching

B is the supervised-token count of the plain arm: the first passing attempt per task with at least one pass, one trajectory per task. Every arm trains on B agentic tokens plus the same replay slice for the same number of optimizer steps.

- Plain SFT (control): as above.
- RS-multi: identical task slots to plain; when a task recurs in a later epoch, a different passing attempt is used. Measures demonstration diversity at a fixed budget.
- Relay (#10027): v0's own turns stay in context with no loss; GLM's turns are trained; passing episodes subsampled to B. Episodes with no teacher turn are dropped.
- Recovery (phase 2): the plain trajectories; 20% receive one or two synthetic failed turns re-rendered in v0's measured error styles plus the real harness error, inserted through the parser; injections carry no loss, so the budget equals B by construction. Waits on a validated injection generator.
- Plateau dropping (#10028, phase 2): the plain trajectories; tokens whose loss has plateaued lose gradient; matched on optimizer steps, with gradient-carrying tokens reported. Waits on the trainer.

Phase 1 is plain, RS-multi and relay.

## Evaluation

Every arm, including plain, runs the retention gate (GSM8K, BFCL-Parity, GPQA-Diamond) and the agentic endpoint (SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.1, TBLite 2.0) under the policy's trial counts and pins. An arm passes when it has no decisive loss against plain on the gate and a decisive win over plain on at least one agentic benchmark with no decisive loss on the others, where decisive is the policy's rule (gap above 1.96 times the combined task-level standard error, each scaled by 1/sqrt(0.9)). One policy run resolves gaps of roughly 4 to 5 points on SWE-bench Verified and 8 to 10 on the terminal benchmarks; unresolved arms are reported with intervals and not promoted. Passing arms, plain and v0 go to the 23-benchmark tournament.

## Learning-rate sweep of the control

Running now, on pilot data (existing Qwen3.6-27B TMax traces and Kimi-2.5 SWE-smith traces, history-reading trials removed), four runs from v0 at 3e-7, 1e-6, 3e-6 and 1e-5, 3 epochs, recipe otherwise fixed. Screens per run: held-out validation loss on 5% of tasks, GSM8K, BFCL-Parity, SWE-bench Verified random-100 and a 100-task TBLite subset. Decision rule, fixed in advance: among rates with no decisive retention loss against v0, the best equal-weight mean of the two agentic screens; ties to the smaller rate. The chosen rate is confirmed once on the real plain-arm data and then frozen for all arms.

## Budget

Core (sweep, generation, phase 1, tournament) about 3,700 to 4,000 H100-hours; phase 2 adds about 2,400, of which 1,700 is an optional 20-epoch plateau comparison. GLM generation runs on the internal service and sandbox CPU and is outside the GPU budget.

## Status and next steps

- Pilot dataset and learning-rate sweep: in progress.
- Task pool, decontamination and package fix: in progress.
- Harness bring-up, one-task dry runs, a 200-task-per-family pass-rate pilot and a relay dry run: in progress. The full 8-attempt generation waits on their results.
- Then: phase-1 training, first-stage evaluation, tournament for passers; phase 2 when its code exists.

Design notes and diagrams are kept in the maintainer's notes and will be attached as results land.

## Decision log

- 2026-10-15: scope cut to SFT only; merging and on-policy distillation dropped. Base set to Snowball v0.
- 2026-10-16: one harness per task family following the policy's scoring agents; GLM 5.3 as the single teacher with regenerated traces instead of reusing Kimi and Qwen traces; RS arm redefined as resampling across epochs after the token-budgeted variant was found to re-weight tasks; task eligibility defined by teacher success only; unfiltered-SFT control dropped; primary endpoint set to the agentic benchmarks with the tournament secondary; git-history leak found in the SWE-smith packages and a strip added to the pool build.

🤖 Teacher generation bring-up: one-task dry runs

## TL;DR

GLM 5.3 now runs end to end in both harnesses (Harbor `016dd78b`, Daytona sandboxes, run from cw-us-east-02a):
- TMax under Terminus-2, with the 65,536 / 16,384 limits from the policy;
- SWE-smith under the mini-swe-agent 2.1.0 adapter, with a 32,768-token window.

**The adapter question is answered.** The mini-swe-agent adapter runs a raw SWE-smith Harbor package unchanged, and the dry-run trace fit inside 32k (largest prompt 13.4k tokens). One trace says nothing about the length distribution; the pilot will measure it.

**The GLM pass on SWE-smith read the fix from git history** (#10212). Before the SWE-smith pass-rate pilot, the packages need the history-stripped repair.

**The pilot has not started.** It waits on a capacity confirmation for the GLM service.

## Per trial

| | TMax `task_000000_5c5b0938` | SWE-smith `swesmith-00003` |
|---|---|---|
| Reward | 0 in the first run, 1 in a rerun | 1 in both runs |
| Model calls | 4 | 16 to 17 |
| Prompt tokens (total / largest) | 9.3k to 10.1k / 3.7k | 145k to 156k (about 93% prefix-cached) / 13.4k |
| Completion tokens (reasoning) | 5.1k to 6.2k (4.2k to 5.2k) | 3.4k to 3.6k (0.5k to 0.8k) |
| Model time | 39 s | 16 s |
| Trial wall time | 42 to 93 s (environment build 3 to 45 s) | 74 to 80 s (verifier 20 to 25 s) |

## Effective generation settings

Both clients send only `model` and `max_tokens=16384`, so GLM runs on the service defaults. GLM 5.3's template then renders `Reasoning Effort: Max`.

Every request is logged by an in-cluster proxy. The log records the settings as sent and the full reply, reasoning included. The proxy also serves `/tokenize` with the `zai-org/GLM-5.3` tokenizer, because the mini-swe-agent context limiter needs it and the relay does not provide it. Its token counts matched the service on every request.

## Transcripts

Both harnesses write Harbor ATIF trajectories:
- **Terminus-2:** each step's message is the JSON action, and the reasoning is in `reasoning_content`.
- **mini-swe-agent:** native `bash` tool calls with `{returncode, output}` observations, but the trajectory **drops GLM's reasoning**. Training rows are therefore rebuilt from the proxy log, which keeps it. That rebuild checks clean on both dry runs.

## What the agent can see

Measured with an oracle-agent probe during the agent phase:

| | TMax (converted) | SWE-smith (raw package) |
|---|---|---|
| `/tests` | absent | absent |
| `/solution` | absent | absent |
| Other task files | none | none |
| Git history | no repository | 944 branches, including `main` and the full history |

The SWE-smith dry-run pass used that history: it ran `git show 614b134:<file>`, then checked its edit against that file. Details are in #10212.

## Other findings

- **TMax is not in Harbor format** in `tasks.zip`. The pool converts it with TMax's own `convert_to_harbor.py` at `hamishivi/tmax@6d3d606c`, minus 181 environments with hidden verifier assets, giving 2,019 tasks.
- **The dry-run TMax task looks flawed.** It runs an OpenMP parallel loop over the outer LU loop with 4 threads, while the test expects the sequential determinant. The task failed once and passed once.

## Next

- **TMax pilot:** 200 tasks x 2 attempts, seed 20261016, drawn uniformly from 1,963 eligible tasks (the pool minus #202's held-out ids). Staged; starts when capacity is confirmed.
- **SWE-smith pilot:** 200 x 2, stratified by repository, on the history-stripped packages.
- **Relay dry run:** 20 tasks per family, with v0 served by the policy serving config. GLM takes over on these triggers:
  - format error: GLM writes one repair turn;
  - context budget at 0.75 of the window: GLM continues to the end;
  - completion claim: v0's reply is withheld and logged, and GLM continues to the end.

Run folders: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/generation/dryrun/{tmax-dry1,tmax-dry2,swe-dry3,swe-dry4,visibility1}`

🤖 TMax pass-rate pilot with GLM 5.3 under Terminus-2: pass@1 0.77, pass@2 0.83 on 200 tasks × 2.

**TL;DR:** GLM 5.3 solves most TMax tasks. Only 1% of trials ended with no reward. The median trajectory is 9.6k tokens, but 12.8% of conversations exceed 32k. 9 of 400 trials (2.25%) went through context summarization, and those cannot become single 32k training rows.

**Setup**
- Tasks: 200 drawn uniformly (seed 20261016) from TMax pool P (#206): 1,918 eligible tasks after all 101 held-out ids were removed.
- Packages: `tmax-packages.parquet` (`allenai/TMax-SFT-16.5K@848e2182` converted with `hamishivi/tmax@6d3d606c`).
- Agent: Terminus-2 at the eval-policy Harbor pin (`marin-community/harbor@016dd78b`), 65,536 input / 16,384 output tokens, agent timeout 1,800 s, Daytona sandboxes.
- Model: GLM 5.3 through the bulk service. Clients send only `model` and `max_tokens=16384`, so the service defaults apply and the chat template renders "Reasoning Effort: Max".
- Concurrency 32. The run took 66 min of wall time (00:19–01:25 UTC).

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Trials | 400 (200 tasks × 2), 0 Harbor retries |
| pass@1 (all trials / graded only) | 0.7725 / 0.7803 |
| pass@2 | 0.825 |
| No reward (infra or agent error before grading) | 4 trials (1.0%): TmuxBatchProtocolError 2, TmuxSessionEndedError 2 |
| Agent timeouts (1,800 s; still graded) | 9 |

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 Relay rounds broken by a preempted student server ([#10237](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10237)).

**Affected rounds**
- TMax relay shard-02 round 1: 198 of 200 trials errored, 14:33-15:13 UTC on 2026-10-17. Moved to `traces/tmax-relay/shard-02/round-1.failed-0a6b03ad`; it will be rerun. It was never published.
- SWE-smith relay shard-00 round 3: 85 of 97 trials errored, from about 08:29 UTC. Its 32 valid rows are published; trials that raised without a GLM reply don't count as relay runs.

I'm checking every other round for a student preemption and will post the full list.

**Cause.** In relay mode, the v0 student runs as a child inference job. When that job was preempted, Iris rescheduled it on another host. The relay proxy kept calling the address resolved once at startup (`lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris.py:682`). Every student call then failed with `httpx.ConnectError`, the agents got HTTP 500, and Harbor still exited 0.

**Fix** (`task/212` @ [`174906474a`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/174906474a8039d1ff8989e8f6d53103242cfec1)):
- On a connection error, the proxy looks up the student's current address and retries for up to 20 minutes.
- The proxy logs its own failures, which used to go unlogged.
- A run fails, with no `_SUCCESS`, when more than 20% of its trials raise without a reply.

The relay lanes are being resubmitted on this commit.

comments.body:
🤖 Decisions for the next data round (v7), 2026-10-19.

1. Regenerate the GLM 5.3 pool at a lower reasoning effort. The max-effort traces caused both phase-1 defects: long reasoning used up the 30k generation window (so half of the passing SWE-smith attempts never reached the submit step) and taught a style that times out TBLite. GLM 5.3's chat template exposes only `low`, `high` and max (`medium` renders as max, and `high` reasoned to the token cap like max in a probe), so a pilot of 200 TMax and 200 SWE-smith tasks x 2 samples at `low` and `high` is running (launched 21:01 UTC) to measure pass rate, clean-pass rate, per-turn reasoning and context use against the max-effort pool. The full k=8 regeneration on pool v5, plus relay rounds, follows at the chosen setting with the same gates.
2. Select demonstrations by clean completion: an attempt counts only if it passed and ended with the agent's own finish (mini-swe-agent submit, Terminus-2 `task_complete`). On the max-effort traces this keeps 919 of 1,995 SWE-smith tasks and 1,475 of 1,914 TMax tasks; the lower-effort traces should keep more.
3. Switch the base to Snowball v0.1 (`open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14`, selected in #10283 under the same policy). Same architecture, tokenizer and template as v0, and without v0's relay SFT graft, so it is a cleaner base for the relay arm. The relay student becomes v0.1 and v0.1 reference screens will be run. The LR sweep result (1e-6, 3 epochs) is carried over rather than repeated.
4. Rebuild all five arms on the new rows, retrain and screen them. The v5 arms above remain the max-effort finding.

Recovery SFT implementation check: the owner obtained the original recovery generation code; the mechanism matches ours (injection points, 1–3 attempts, Terminus-2 reply template and parser, teacher-authored failed turns, masking). Two rendering details from it are adopted (varied renders per error style; streaks of the same style, with rates measured on v0's own trajectories: 56.6% same style, 0% identical); we keep trained tokens equal to plain's.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 **Update 2026-10-22: every SFT arm trained on the GLM 5.3 traces scores below its parent on the agentic screens. Two next steps: re-run the cheap arms on the contributor (Kimi/Qwen) traces, and check the learning rate on the real rows.**

## Results on the GLM 5.3 traces

Screens are SWE-bench Verified random-100 and the TBLite 100-task subset (solved out of 100; TBLite timeouts count as failures), GSM8K and BFCL-Parity for retention. "Composite" is our screening mean (SWE + TBLite)/2, shown as a range when trials were unscored for infrastructure reasons; it is a bound, not a confidence interval. HIGH and LOW are the GLM reasoning-effort settings used to generate the traces; rows are token-matched per arm.

| model | parent | rows | SWE-bench r100 (submits) | TBLite-100 | GSM8K | BFCL | composite |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| parent v0.1 | – | – | 26 (36) | 23 | 91.1 | 32/123 | 24.5-25.0 |
| plain | v0.1 | HIGH | 13 (4) | 8 | 92.3 | 67/123 | 10.5-11.5 |
| plain | v0.1 | LOW | 17 (27) | 12 | 91.7 | 55/121 | 14.5-18.0 |
| relay | v0.1 | LOW | 25 (25) | 15 | 92.9 | 64/123 | 20.0-21.0 |
| parent v0 | – | – | 33 (56) | 20 | 85.2 | 27/122 | 26.5-27.0 |
| plain | v0 | HIGH | 17 (3) | 9 | 87.7 | 44/122 | 13.0-17.5 |
| plain, cut to the relay arm's token count | v0 | HIGH | 13 (6) | 11 | 91.1 | 54/123 | 12.0-12.5 |
| RS-multi | v0 | HIGH | 11 (6) | 10 | 89.9 | 41/123 | 10.5-11.0 |
| recovery | v0 | HIGH | 12 (4) | 9 | 88.5 | 48/123 | 10.5-11.0 |
| relay | v0 | HIGH | 13 (1) | 14 | 89.0 | 48/123 | 13.5-14.0 |
| plateau dropping | v0 | HIGH | 14 (6) | 13 | 89.8 | 49/123 | 13.5 |

What the data say:
- Every arm is below its parent on SWE-bench and TBLite and above it on GSM8K and BFCL. The regression is specific to the agentic tasks.
- Paired per-task differences on the frozen task lists (task bootstrap, 95%): no HIGH-row method differs from plain on either screen (SWE-bench -3 to -6 [about -13, +4]; TBLite 0 to +3 [about -6, +9]). Relay on the LOW rows beats plain on the LOW rows on SWE-bench by +8 [+1, +16], the only method-versus-twin interval that excludes zero; on TBLite +1 [-6, +7]. Every student is below its parent on SWE-bench (HIGH-row arms -13 to -22, intervals exclude zero; LOW relay -1 [-10, +8]) and most are below on TBLite.
- Relay on the LOW rows is therefore the strongest arm (25 SWE-bench vs the parent's 26), with the caveat that its recipe differs from plain's (963 vs 675 updates at equal tokens, student prefix masked) and that LOW rows hold 11.6M supervised tokens per epoch against HIGH's 19.4M.
- Mechanism, measured on trajectories: students keep the rows' per-step style (about 120 tokens per step, same command mix) but take about twice the rows' steps, run into the 32k window (75-97% of episodes) and rarely submit (HIGH-trained 3-6%, LOW-trained about 25%, parents 36-56%). Submitting is where the score comes from.
- The two parents are not distinguishable on the frozen task lists: paired SWE-bench difference v0 minus v0.1 = +7 [-2, +16], TBLite -3 [-12, +6] (task bootstrap). Of the 49 TBLite tasks where v0.1 timed out, v0 solved 3, so v0.1's timeouts are mostly hard tasks, not lost score (#10338: tripling the limit changed its score by one task).

Limits: one run per arm, 100 tasks per screen (about 4 points of standard error), TBLite timeout-bound for every student.

## Next step 1: the same cheap arms on the contributor traces

The one run of this recipe that beat its parent was the learning-rate sweep's 1e-6 run on the pilot traces (Qwen3.6-27B TMax episodes and Kimi-2.5 SWE-smith episodes, the data the contributors' original experiments used): composite 31.0-32.0 against v0's 26.5-27.0, TBLite 29 vs 20. That run used the sweep's sampler and exposure, not the arm recipe, so it is suggestive, not a control. The pilot rows also look different from the GLM rows: 14 steps per episode at 246 tokens per step with 28% reasoning tokens (HIGH: 25 steps, 120 tokens, 39%), and they are in Terminus-2 format, which never contains the mini-swe-agent submit command, yet that student kept 40% submits.

Plan: convert the pilot traces to the arm row format and train plain, RS-multi and recovery from v0.1 at 1e-6 under the arm recipe, plus plain from v0 as the bridge to the sweep. v0.1 is the base because it carries no relay graft and v0 was trained on about half of the pilot SWE tasks through the relay data grafted into it. Known limits: the Kimi SWE set has one trajectory per task, so RS-multi runs on TMax only; recovery needs an error style for Qwen's native tool calls; about 1,500 pilot SWE tasks have only the pilot's own decontamination check. Target: plain results within a day of the rows, the other two a day later.

## Next step 2: learning rate on the real rows

The sweep tied 3e-7, 1e-6 and 3e-6 on the pilot rows and 1e-6 was frozen without the planned confirmation on real plain rows. Two checks are running: plain SFT on the LOW v0 rows at 3e-7, paired against the 1e-6 twin (same rows, parent and schedule), to test whether gentler updates preserve more of the parent; and a screen of the HIGH plain v0.1 epoch-2 checkpoint against its final, as an update-dose check. A higher rate is not excluded but is the less likely direction given the sweep.

Also in flight: plain, relay and plateau on the LOW rows from v0, and RS-multi and recovery on the LOW rows from v0.1, to complete the LOW comparison on both parents. Models so far are on the Hub under `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-SFT-Shootout-*` (private). Design: [SFT comparison doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/13duCN6reb7KVLhBi8TszTL1EYKeaV3SEMQhl9IJCZSM/edit).

issues.body:
Add NVIDIA's [Skill2Env](https://github.com/NVlabs/Skill2Env) to the RL Data Atlas with a reproducible assessment that helps people decide whether to use the tasks. This issue tracks registration, conversion, validation, and publication. Training integration and upstream grader repair remain separate work.

Current status (2026-10-22): catalog registration (#10120) and Harbor Hub acquisition (#10198) are merged. QUICK conversion in #10154 is ready for human review at `4b45b34ebf`. The full-release run confirmed 7,452 converted tasks and 44 exclusions. Runnable SAMPLE/FULL campaigns remain unfinished; live Atlas publication has not been verified. The earlier #9632 implementation is superseded.

The inventory entry is `Harbor Hub:skill2env`, pinned to release version 1.0.1 / revision 2 with 7,496 tasks, digest `sha256:bef4f739bde8d865af04c04a2cb1c84ecad83b52dd558f4d582dd46c7933666c`.

Completed validation:

- The full-release QUICK driver at `4b45b34ebf`, recipe revision 10, processed cached packages in 75 batches: 7,452 converted, 42 `native_outputs` exclusions, and 2 `native_workspace` exclusions. There were no unexpected failures. Every converted TaskSpec was read back and every uploaded batch archive was checksum-verified.
- Native and converted grading matched across 146 controls for all 29 digest-pinned capture exceptions. Controls cover initial state, reference solutions, corrupted state, deleted state, and empty submissions, plus one symlink control. Both reward components and scalar means matched. One native reference solution scored 0.98; conversion reproduced that value. Matching rewards do not establish grader correctness.
- All 22 focused tests and mechanical lint pass. CI at `4b45b34ebf` has 18 successful checks and 20 skipped, with none failed or pending. The latest independent review of that exact commit found no actionable code defects. Its PR-description cleanup is applied.

The 44 exclusions remain explicit because the current runtime cannot preserve their execution contracts or validation found a mismatch. They include filesystem metadata, live-process and startup requirements, inaccessible state, and incomplete Git metadata in a cached export. Seven candidates failed symlink/executable-state comparisons. The Go-based `yeet` task scored 1.0 natively and 0.0 after conversion and stays excluded. The cached `lsp-edit-symbol` failure has not been established as an upstream dataset defect. The adapter introduces no new service fixture or privileged capture mechanism.

Remaining work:

- [ ] Human review and merge of #10154.
- [ ] Resolve and pin actor/verifier images, configure native resource limits, and validate the runnable campaign path. QUICK still retains unresolved build contexts.
- [ ] Run a bounded SAMPLE campaign to assess execution, grading, task quality, and model difficulty. Full-corpus conversion and the selected Docker controls do not complete this assessment.
- [ ] Publish the inventory through a curation campaign and verify the live Atlas source entry. This can proceed independently of runnable integration.
- [ ] Publish and verify the assessment and evidence in Atlas, then close this intake issue.

<details>

The record below is preserved for its evaluation evidence and implementation history. Status statements, integration questions, and checklists in this section refer to the former #9632 approach and are superseded by the current status above.

Add NVIDIA's [Skill2Env](https://github.com/NVlabs/Skill2Env) to the [RL Data Atlas](https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/fb11c931-5861-4878-8bb5-a964d652b45f/) with an assessment that helps people decide whether to use the tasks. This issue tracks dataset intake, validation and publication. Training integration and repairing the dataset's grader are separate work.

The target is the official [Harbor Hub release](https://hub.harborframework.com/datasets/skill2env/skill2env), revision 2, containing 7,496 tasks. Harbor shows the tags `latest` and `v1.0`; the same release's version field is `1.0.1`. These labels refer to the same content. The paper's private S2EBench evaluation set is separate.

Current status: implementation and sampled validation are prepared in PR #9632, now ready for review. The proposed Atlas rating is "Some issues" because one task's grader was shown to reject valid tests. This rating is not yet published. The official release and its grader remain unchanged; the investigation used two temporary copies with modified reference answers.

The intake can finish with a documented "Some issues" rating. Existing Atlas policy permits the standard Small/Large/Hosted model difficulty comparison only for sources rated "Good", so no difficulty comparison was launched. That is an eligibility decision, not an estimate that these tasks are easy or hard. The three-task quality sample does not establish quality across the full dataset.

Evaluation scope: reported rewards come from the released executable graders. The release also includes written rubrics; the paper's additional LLM rubric-scoring layer was not run or validated here ([§§3.2.2 and 4.2](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2609.reinforcing-agents-collective-skills.pdf)). Atlas's GLM-5.3 quality audit separately reviews tasks and graders and does not contribute to those rewards.

The PR contains the implementation and concise design rationale. The evidence and integration review questions below support the assessment. The author has marked the PR ready; Ben's Atlas integration review is still pending. The proposed sequence is review, merge, publish, then verify the live entry; this issue stays open through that verification.

### Integration questions for review

- Catalog design: add checked-in Harbor release registrations as an extension to merged #9518. To assess a newer release, a contributor would update the registration through a Marin PR. Atlas refresh would read that registration; it would not automatically switch releases. Evaluation jobs download tasks separately.
- Runtime dependency: retain the review runner's existing MarinSkyRL result adapter and checkout metadata. The catalog entry needs no training registration, but the runner still has this dependency. Review whether to keep it or separate the Harbor runner from MarinSkyRL before landing.
- Agent setup: use Atlas's Terminus-2 with checksum-pinned tools installed offline, preserving the tasks' network restrictions and resource limits. The paper used Pi; these measurements evaluate the Atlas setup.
- Evaluation budget: the sample used a 50-turn limit inherited from Atlas's example configuration. Two of three attempts reached that limit before signaling completion. Review whether this budget is sufficient for initial intake or whether a larger-budget follow-up is needed.
- Scores: preserve all native reward components from the released executable graders, report their arithmetic mean, and count a full pass only when every component reaches one within numerical tolerance. The paper's additional LLM rubric reward was not run. Atlas's separate LLM quality audit does not contribute to these scores.
- Shared tooling: keep the review-output validation, provenance, evidence-retention and provider-call fixes here, or split them into prerequisite PRs.
- Assessment scope: accept the seeded three-task sample as initial intake evidence. It does not establish quality or difficulty across all 7,496 tasks.

Done when:

- [x] Identify the official release and record its task count, source links and license scope in the proposed registration.
- [x] Run the sampled quality review and preserve the original solver, grader and review evidence.
- [x] Assess eligibility for the standard difficulty comparison; currently ineligible under the "Good"-only rule.
- [ ] Review and merge #9632.
- [ ] Reconcile the currently deployed Atlas source with Ben and agree on who will publish the update.
- [ ] Publish and verify the source entry, dated assessment and grading-problem record in Atlas, then close this intake issue.

<summary>Evaluation results, diagnostic reproduction and evidence identifiers</summary>

The official dataset accompanies [Reinforcing Agents with Collective Skills](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2609.reinforcing-agents-collective-skills). The registered release digest is `sha256:bef4f739bde8d865af04c04a2cb1c84ecad83b52dd558f4d582dd46c7933666c`. Project-owned code is Apache-2.0; third-party task assets retain their own terms.

Sampled evaluation:

Three tasks were selected with seed 42 from all 7,496 pinned release tasks. Every reference-solution reward component was 1 and every no-op component was 0. Task checksums match across those controls and the original GLM-5.3 attempts. All three model attempts reached the native grader without an execution exception; none achieved a full pass.

| Sampled task | Mean component reward | Agent outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ai-seo | 0.93 | Declared completion |
| api-design-reviewer | 0.00 | Used all 50 turns; did not declare completion |
| property-based-testing | 0.25 | Used all 50 turns; did not declare completion |

Scores describe performance within a 50-turn budget. We have not tested whether additional turns improve the two unfinished attempts.

The solver used Terminus-2, GLM-5.3 on Together, Low reasoning effort, and 65,536-total/16,384-output token limits. The Atlas quality-review panel uses GLM-5.3 for three judgments per task and task/source syntheses. All 555 trace-section reviews and 16 original records pass content, schema, reference and evidence-hash checks. The 246 original native artifact files remain byte-identical.

Grader diagnostic:

The task `task_property-based-testing_2kbxlnww` asks the agent to write property tests for a software-version comparison API. A separate diagnostic checked whether its grader wrongly penalizes valid self-comparison tests. Harbor's "oracle agent" runs the supplied reference solution; it is not another model.

The task was pinned at digest `c193f032e03538d875efd6a54026a39621329c2bd88614dab0160b256ed8b4a7`, using official Harbor runner commit `bf991e490394ef9c3250a6db2bc5cbda903cb4c3`. These identifiers make the diagnostic reproducible.

| Reference answer used | Mean native reward | Reference tests | Native mutation result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Authors' original answer | 1.00 | 11 pass | 12/12 killed |
| Same answer with direct self-comparison tests | 0.25 | 12 pass | Skipped by static gate |
| Same tests expressed through a variable alias | 1.00 | 12 pass | 12/12 killed |

To reproduce in a temporary copy, append this property to the reference `solution/test_properties.py`, then run the unchanged native grader through Harbor's oracle agent:

```python
@CI_SETTINGS
@example(Version(1, 2, 3))
@given(valid_versions)
def test_version_reflexivity(version):
    assert version == version
    assert version <= version
    assert version >= version
```

For the equivalent passing control, assign `same_version = version` inside the function and use `same_version` as each comparison's left operand. The grader's `is_self_comparison` compares operand syntax trees; its `no_self_comparison` gate blocks mutation testing for the direct form. The documented task contract does not prohibit valid reflexivity properties on overloaded comparisons.

Only `solution/test_properties.py` in the two temporary diagnostic copies changed. The official release, the grader and the original evaluation artifacts are preserved. All three diagnostic trials completed without an execution exception. They do not replace the original GLM score or establish whether its answer would pass the mutation threshold.

This grading defect supports the prepared "Some issues" assessment. A separate review-panel allegation of leaked SEO helpers was false: the saved trajectory shows the solver creating those helpers. The supplemental review retains the original opinions and replaces their source-level conclusion with the confirmed grading finding. Editable API verifier imports remain a separate concern without a demonstrated exploit.

Evidence and corrections:

Diagnostic job: `/exedev/skill2env-reflexivity-diagnostic-20261002-145621`. Verified diagnostic archive SHA-256: `356b88a8d0c7da1258fbdd669f63d2592991530509571539d90cadc40535a8bb`. Supplemental review SHA-256: `d27b01d25fd27933a1d25a085e65d89b4209afe778f32261a133f3e83c4de79e`.

Independent code review found two problems in the Atlas contribution: omitted trajectory files during publication, and failure to retire the final Harbor registration. Both were fixed in 8df5a15087. These fixes change Atlas tooling, not the Skill2Env grader. A publisher check now retains all nine referenced Harbor summarization files that were missing.

Eight epoch review dates were repaired using native completion timestamps and matching provider-response creation timestamps. The 573 epoch evidence-retrieval references now record their October 2 hash reverification; their original retrieval times are unknown. Original grades, judge opinions and source artifacts remain preserved. No model or native solver runs were repeated for these metadata corrections.

Corrected primary collection SHA-256: `25028bccfca5c246390665e73d8f5cc22a4c6b84a7ea85f4e15169483f7b2da1`. Original collection SHA-256: `e1c4b0befca4292ac8b0afff16a83c29c08278bf627cf81d769e25002b4545e6`. The corrected collection includes the original collection and correction manifests. Supplemental evidence distinguishes the full 7,496-task release from the runner's three staged tasks.

Publication:

Evidence and the publication plan are retained locally; neither the source nor its rating is live in Atlas. Deployed applet revision 58 contains 9,668 more bytes than the merged package (195,096 versus 185,428), although all seven frontend assets match. Obtain and reconcile its deployed manifest/backend source before replacing the applet.

On publication, add the confirmed grading defect to the source's review pool and `catalog_verifier_issues`. Closing this intake issue does not resolve that defect. Clearing its Atlas flag would require a validated fix and fresh review as separate follow-up work.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Implementation validation</summary>

Implementation validation before the Loom follow-up:

All 61 affected local tests and lint passed at `8df5a15087`. Its 17 applicable CI checks passed, including Marina's database suite; 12 were skipped. The publisher check retains all nine previously omitted referenced trajectory files. Backend-factory, migration and browser execution were not validated locally.

At `cc560d56eb`, documentation lint, an isolated Atlas-page build and the applicable GitHub CI checks passed. The local full-site documentation build failed on `ignore_init_summary` on both this branch and base `3ee6cc3e05`.

The Loom follow-up declares the serialized reward schema with `TypedDict` and marks intentionally unused test-callback arguments. It preserves reward calculation and the JSON fields. The nine directly affected local review tests, required lint and focused type check pass. All 17 applicable CI checks pass at `287291cbb4`, including Marina's database suite. The local affected-test runner requires at least two workers, so the focused tests ran serially with the complete default marker exclusions.

The PR retains concise rationale for the Harbor origin, release pinning, retained runtime dependency, scoring, evaluation limits, Harbor logging options, HTTP client identity and Qwen documentation correction. Longer validation details and the review questions live here.

</details>

**Relevant code**

# Skill2Env Atlas contribution

## Design

Create `agent/YYYYMMDD-fix-9630` from the latest #9518 head and open a separate PR against that branch. Register one `Skill2Env:skill2env` source row from a pinned Harbor package release, with the package version or digest, exact task count and count method, source and verifier provenance, links to the official Hub and repository, and license information supported by the released package and its source inventory. Resolve the immutable package identifier and enumerate task IDs before coding the row; do not use `latest` or infer a corpus-wide Apache-2.0 license from the code license. Catalog refresh should retain the pinned row without downloading task archives or silently advancing it.

Extend the Atlas origin list, public table and details, and refresh status for Skill2Env. Use the existing source/review tables so changed data or verifier revisions make prior ratings historical. Adapt the Harbor review route and schema to record its actual Harbor checkout, task bytes, and verifier implementation without requiring unrelated MarinSkyRL source provenance. Keep the native `tests/test.sh` result distinct from the qualitative rubric and the three independent reviewer judgments; preserve solver trajectory, verifier output, judge responses, sample IDs, seed, and dated source synthesis through publication.

Run the standard seeded quality sample against the pinned Harbor tasks and publish its rating and evidence. If it is Good, run the same task IDs through the Atlas Small (Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct), Large (Qwen3.5-122B-A10B), and Hosted (GLM-5.3) arms under the current protocol enforced by `app.py`; use its judge-verifier variant only if the native verifier calls a model. Record checkpoint identities, generation settings, per-arm solved/verified/attempted counts, and infrastructure failures separately. Publish difficulty only when the protocol matches and the source review remains current. Link the dated Atlas review and dependent implementation PR here.

## Validation and risk

Test the pinned count and links, refresh idempotence, revision-based staleness, Harbor-only provenance and publication, and public filtering. Validate the applet and inspect the public page after publication. Native Harbor execution needs a Docker-capable environment; the first sampled run must establish that the released package and its verifier work before any model comparison. Keep failed executions as evidence and out of solve-rate denominators until their status is resolved.

## Open question

Does the Hub expose an immutable package digest and task-level license metadata for this release? If it exposes only a version tag, archive a task-ID and file-hash manifest with the review so the counted and executed populations can be checked later.

issues.body:
Snowball/Grug checkpoints back to the 09.21 Datakit SFT model sometimes write more than one thinking segment in a single assistant message. The usual form is a think block followed by a second segment closed by a stray `<|end_think|>` with no matching `<|start_think|>`. Smartie RL step 14 also stacks complete near-duplicate blocks with nothing between them:

```
<|start_think|>We need to see the files first. Let's list them and examine content.<|end_think|><|start_think|>We need to inspect the files to understand the corrections. Let's list and view them.<|end_think|><|start_think|>We need to see the content. Let's run ls to see files.<|end_think|><|start_think|>I'll list the files in the workspace.<|end_think|>
```

The `grug` reasoning parser moves only the first segment into `reasoning`. It splits at the first `<|start_think|>` and the first `<|end_think|>` ([`basic_parsers.py:157`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/3a054c458ca8a32609ba2bc578c4d9b93eabb395/vllm/reasoning/basic_parsers.py#L157), inherited by [`grug_reasoning_parser.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/3a054c458ca8a32609ba2bc578c4d9b93eabb395/vllm/reasoning/grug_reasoning_parser.py)). Later segments stay in `content` with raw think tags, so users and LLM judges see them. Tool calls after the segments still parse.

The same Smartie conversations also show long thinking-only loops that hit the token limit with an empty reply, for example `\n\nNow.` repeated 7,986 times.

Reproduce:
1. Open case `108de5fc` in the [Smartie step 14 vs Qwen 3.6 comparison](https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/25f504c6-c6fb-4e14-8401-07dd8e6fbfba/v/28/?run=smartie-rl-step14-vs-qwen36-20261019-v3-final4#108de5fc029a4b65adb39205bdae818e).
2. Round 0, first assistant message: the reply text contains four stacked think blocks before the `ls` tool call.
3. Rounds 2 and 3: the turns end at `finish_reason=length` with no reply.

Expected: at most one think block per assistant message, as rendered by `MARIN_CHAT_TEMPLATE` (`lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_template.py:108`).

comments.author: davidlundgren
comments.body:
🤖 The pretraining data teaches the "close, keep reasoning, close again" habit. It comes mostly from one SWE-agent source, `swe-zero-12m`.

### Pretraining scan
I read one row group of normalized shard 0 for every source in the base mixture (`gs://marin-us-central2/datakit/store_8ac06c74`, 114 sources) and counted think tags per document.

- **The pattern:** in about 0.8% of `swe-zero-12m` documents, every assistant turn is `THOUGHT: <reasoning> </thinking>` followed by a bash action, with no opening tag. Some turns close twice or three times: reasoning, `</thinking>`, more reasoning, `</thinking>` again. A second shard gave the same rate (15/1,936 vs 15/1,944 documents).
- **Share of training:** `swe-zero-12m` is about 4% of training tokens and was seen about 4 times. Documents with this shape are about 0.04% of all tokens, roughly 5M stray close tags in total. Over ~10T tokens that is about 5×10⁻⁷ per token (one per ~2M), and about 7% of all think-tag exposure; balanced blocks outnumber it roughly 14:1. It is a single template repeated about 15 times per document, across about 94k SWE-agent transcripts seen about 4 times. So the prior is weak but consistent, and domain-matched to the leaking evals. SFT suppresses it without eliminating it (0.6–2.5%), and RL amplifies it (9%+).
- **Bare `</think>`:** `davinci-dev/env-native` has `</think>` with no opening tag in 3% of its documents. It is only 0.07% of the mixture.
- **Clean sources:** the multi-turn reasoning sources (nemotron-terminal, the nemotron SFT sets, gpt-oss-rollouts) have one balanced think block per turn. General web text has no tags.
- **Phases:** pretraining, cooldown and the step-156k→157k context extension that the SFT started from all draw from this one store. Only the bucket weights change between phases, so this data is present right up to the base checkpoint.

The base checkpoint (`open-athena/snowball-67b-a2b-base-262k-qk175-skew8`) shows the same shape. In its SWE-bench eval it emitted plain-text `</think>` 6,546 times and `<think>` 307 times across 595 agent messages.

The base model writes these as plain-text tags, while SFT and RL models use the `<|end_think|>` special token, so the habit has to carry over across forms. That is plausible but not shown. A few-shot base test is running to measure it.

### Rendering parity: ruled out
For the main eval path (pi agent, `reasoning_parser: null`, hermes tools), the inference prompt matches the SFT rendering token for token, in simulated and real bixbench trajectories. The model also leaks on turn 0, before it has any history. The grug parser with streaming does garble history once a leak exists: `extract_reasoning_streaming` drops lone think tokens. That is a secondary bug, not the cause.

### RL amplifies it
The answer extractor (`final_answer_text`) keeps the text after the last close marker, and SWE grading parses tool calls across the whole completion. Multi-segment completions therefore get full reward. Nothing pushes back once RL samples the pattern.

### Examples

issues.title: [snowball] Grug checkpoints emit extra think segments that leak into replies

issues.author: davidlundgren
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Not started. This tests whether one short SFT pass over the 10.05 checkpoint's own samples, with each malformed reasoning span repaired, removes extra think segments without lowering pass rate. If it does, consumers get a patched 10.05 instead of a full SFT re-run, which took 126 hours on 1,024 TPU v4 chips.

## Description

`open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05` (revision `8c76b22`) sometimes writes more than one reasoning segment in one assistant message: a stray `<|end_think|>` after the first block, or back-to-back blocks (#10400). This happens in 0.6% of thinking messages on bixbench-pi and 3.2% on bfclparity-pi, and RL raises the rate to 9.1% (Smartie RL step 14). #10518, #10519 and #10520 stop new data and RL from teaching or rewarding the habit, but the 10.05 checkpoint keeps it.

A re-run of the 10.05 SFT would cost about 129k TPU v4 chip-hours. The W&B run `grug-67b-sft-20260929-special-token-lr-full-ab-4750-grouped` (project `marin_moe_sft`) took 125.9 h for 4,750 steps on 1,024 chips at 94.9 s/step, plus 5.2 h in two crashed starts.

The patch trains on the model's own samples. Off-policy rows change think behavior quickly: four updates at 1e-5 on GLM-written rows cut closed think blocks from 255 of 284 to 53 of 387 ([curriculum SFT README](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/experiments/post_training/curriculum_sft/README.md#L89-L101)). Training on clean samples alone gives a weak signal when only about 2% of samples are malformed. A repaired sample differs from the model's own output only at the malformed span, so its loss targets that decision.

## Hypothesis or Goal

One pass over at most 2,000 rows of repaired and clean samples, at a learning rate of at most 1e-5, cuts the held-out violation rate at least 10x and keeps held-out pass rate within 2 points of 10.05.

## Design

1. Baseline from stored samples (CPU only). #10000 sampled 10.05 8 times per SWE and terminal pivot prompt, with thinking on, temperature 1.0, special tokens kept and no reasoning parser ([runs.py](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/33f37f1c9a36368102d3c2d4c5d13beddb8a2263/experiments/post_training/pivotrl/runs.py#L128-L139)). The raw messages are in `message_json` under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/dml/pivotrl/<candidates>/pass-rates/grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft-262k-20261005/2026.10.09/`. Classify each sample as well-formed (one `<|start_think|>` at the start and one `<|end_think|>`), stray end, back-to-back, or orphan close, and count `finish_reason=length` separately. If fewer than 0.5% of samples are malformed, switch to tool-use chat prompts like bfclparity-pi.
2. Rows (CPU only), from training candidates only. A repaired row takes a malformed sample that did not hit the token limit. Its reasoning is everything before the last `<|end_think|>`, with inner think tokens replaced by a blank line. Its reply and tool calls are unchanged. A clean row is a well-formed sample from the same prompts, unchanged. Use equal numbers of repaired and clean rows, keep samples whatever their task score, and put the loss on the final assistant turn only.
3. Train three arms from 10.05, one pass each, with an export at mid-pass and one at the end:

   | Arm | Rows | Learning rate |
   |---|---|---|
   | T-low | repaired + clean | 1e-6 |
   | T-high | repaired + clean | 1e-5 |
   | C-high | clean only, same row count | 1e-5 |

   Two trainers fit. The arm trainer in #10327 (prebuilt `input_ids` and `loss_weights`, batch 16 × 32k, constant learning rate, 4×8 H100) needs a 10.05 entry in its [`PARENTS`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/01d104874e0c3c20fc38a65645b466d3c02bde8b/experiments/post_training/agentic_sweep/arms.py#L94-L107) table and rows in its manifest format. The PivotRL SFT path in #10000 already trains on the final turn of pivot prompts.
4. Measure on the held-out pivot rows, 4 samples per row, with the same settings for 10.05 and every arm (`heldout_baseline_step` and `heldout_eval_step` in #10000). The primary metric is the violation rate. The guards are pass rate, the share of samples that close their span, and the `finish_reason=length` rate. Sample enough rows for 10.05 to show at least 20 violations. Then run bfclparity-pi and bixbench-pi on the best arm and compare with the 10.05 runs from 2026-10-17.

Decision rule:
- Success: the violation rate falls at least 10x and its 95% interval excludes the 10.05 rate. Pass rate stays within 2 points, and the span-closing and length-stop rates do not get worse.
- If T-low succeeds, publish 10.05 with the patch as the base for consumers and add the patch to the post-training recipe.
- If T-high succeeds and C-high does not, the repair is what works. Adopt T-high if the guards hold.
- If C-high also succeeds, clean on-policy samples are enough and the repair step can go.
- If no arm succeeds, try a format reward in RL (#10520) before an SFT re-run.

If the patch works, repeat T-low on v0.1 (`open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14`, the base in #10213), which has extra segments in 9.1% of thinking messages.

Estimated cost: 100–150 H100-hours, about one day. Each arm takes 20–25 H100-hours, mostly model loading, compilation and export; its 65M padded tokens train in minutes. Held-out sampling takes about 8 H100-hours per checkpoint, and bfclparity-pi plus bixbench-pi take 20–40 H100-hours for one arm.

## Status

Not started.

## Links

* Logbook: this issue
* W&B Report:
* Important updates:
* Parent: #10400. Trainers: #10327, #10000. Related: #10428 (format SFT on Hero).

## Decision Log

- 2026-10-22: Patch the existing 10.05 checkpoint before considering an SFT re-run, which costs about 129k TPU v4 chip-hours. Train on repaired on-policy rows, for the reasons in the description.

## Conclusion

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

The 10.05 checkpoint can emit extra reasoning delimiters, and the `grug` parser leaves later segments in reply content (#10400). The stored PivotRL samples retain special tokens and `message_json`, so the first measurement and row construction can use the existing artifacts without new inference. No open PR targets #10521; the relevant trainers, #10000 and #10327, are still draft PRs, and #10327 currently accepts only v0/v0.1 parents and its sweep-specific arm manifest.

**Relevant code**
- [`runs.py#L101-L139`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/33f37f1c9a36368102d3c2d4c5d13beddb8a2263/experiments/post_training/pivotrl/runs.py#L101-L139) — pinned 10.05 model and thinking-on sampling.
- [`pass_rates.py#L73-L101`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/33f37f1c9a36368102d3c2d4c5d13beddb8a2263/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/pass_rates.py#L73-L101) — stored message and stop-reason fields.
- [`sft_templates.py#L23-L35`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/33f37f1c9a36368102d3c2d4c5d13beddb8a2263/experiments/post_training/pivotrl/sft_templates.py#L23-L35) — final-turn loss mask.
- [`sft.py#L622-L667`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/33f37f1c9a36368102d3c2d4c5d13beddb8a2263/experiments/post_training/pivotrl/sft.py#L622-L667) — matched held-out sampling.
- [`arms.py#L82-L121`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d23b8c9a94ea9c2c593f185287f28b86676f6a48/experiments/post_training/agentic_sweep/arms.py#L82-L121) — current arm and parent restrictions.

# Proposed Fix

1. Audit the stored 10.05 SWE and terminal samples on CPU. Split by candidate row before selecting training examples; classify each assistant message by delimiter pattern and count `finish_reason=length` separately. Report counts by prompt family and sample ID. If violations are below 0.5%, sample tool-use prompts as the issue specifies. Size the held-out set to show at least 20 baseline violations.
2. Build a versioned manifest and at most 2,000 final-turn examples from training candidates only: equal repaired and unchanged clean rows, plus a clean-only comparator with the same row count. Exclude length stops, preserve reply text and tool calls, record source sample IDs and before/after delimiter counts, and test tokenized renderings for each malformed class and the loss mask.
3. Extend the Grug path in #10000 after its #9933 dependency is settled. It already pins 10.05, masks earlier turns, and measures held-out pass rates; configure one pass at 1e-6 and 1e-5 on repaired plus clean rows and one pass at 1e-5 on clean rows, with mid-pass and final exports. Check the actual GPU-hour estimate before launch because this path currently allocates 8×8 H100 rather than the 4×8 arm trainer cited in the issue. Coordinate changes with #10000 instead of opening a parallel trainer PR.
4. Evaluate 10.05 and every export on the same held-out rows with four samples per row and identical serving settings. Report violation classes, pass rate, closed-span share, and length-stop rate with 95% intervals clustered by prompt. Apply the issue's 10× reduction and 2-point pass-rate guards before running bfclparity-pi and bixbench-pi on the selected arm. Publish artifact paths, exact checkpoint revisions, and the adoption decision here.

issues.author: davidlundgren
issues.body:
Part of #10400. The Marin chat format allows zero, one or several reasoning spans in an assistant turn. A grader therefore cannot treat a second span as an error, and training rows can teach any of these shapes.

Under `Reasoning: /think`, two paths produce turns that do not start with exactly one span:

- [`_inference_messages`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_render.py#L69-L79) joins the analysis messages of a turn into `content`, each wrapped in its own `<|start_think|>…<|end_think|>` by [`_assistant_content`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_render.py#L33-L41). A turn with two analysis messages renders two spans. The 10.05 SFT mix has 23 turns with two spans, all back-to-back pairs in `nemotron_sft_v3/math_v2` ([scan](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10400#issuecomment-6326229373)).
- [`MARIN_CHAT_TEMPLATE`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_template.py#L106-L114) renders a span only when `reasoning_content` is non-empty. [`chat_normalize`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_normalize.py#L276-L278) turns on `/think` for the whole conversation when any assistant message has analysis, so a call-only turn in that conversation renders with no span.

Target format: under `/think`, every assistant turn starts with exactly one span, which is empty when the turn has no reasoning. Under `/nothink`, no turn has a span. An undefined reasoning mode keeps the current behavior. Each checkpoint serves the chat template stored in its own repository, so existing checkpoints keep the current template.

Done when:
- `MARIN_CHAT_TEMPLATE` is the only code that emits think tokens, and SFT rendering and serving both produce the target format.
- `CHAT_RENDER_VERSION` is bumped from `marin-v3`.
- Parity cases in `tests/test_marin_tokenizer.py` cover an empty span, a turn with two analysis messages, `/nothink`, a call-only turn, and a conversation that mixes them.
- A new `marin-community/marin-tokenizer` revision carries the template.
- An audit of the rerendered SFT stores finds no `/think` assistant turn with zero spans or more than one.
- `docs/tutorials/add-chat-dataset.md` describes the format.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

`_inference_messages()` folds adjacent assistant messages into one turn, while `_assistant_content()` wraps each analysis message separately. `MARIN_CHAT_TEMPLATE` emits a span only for nonempty `reasoning_content`; `chat_normalize` sets `/think` for the whole conversation when any assistant turn has analysis. The existing parity table already compares Datakit text with tokenizer output, but it does not cover multiple analysis messages or an empty span. No open PR directly addresses #10519; #10520 covers the separate RL grader.

**Relevant code**
- [`chat_render.py#L33-L79`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_render.py#L33-L79) — analysis wrapping and turn folding
- [`chat_template.py#L106-L115`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_template.py#L106-L115) — conditional span emission
- [`chat_normalize.py#L275-L278`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_normalize.py#L275-L278) — conversation-level mode
- [`test_marin_tokenizer.py#L261-L433`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/tests/test_marin_tokenizer.py#L261-L433) — renderer/tokenizer parity

# Reasoning span format

A `/think` assistant turn will start with one `<|start_think|>...<|end_think|>` pair, including an empty pair for turns without analysis. `/nothink` will emit no pair. An omitted mode and other custom mode strings will retain the current conditional behavior.

## Challenges and risks

Consecutive analysis messages need one `reasoning_content` value. Moving analysis before commentary also changes relative order if a source interleaves those channels; the rerender audit should count such records separately. A template change invalidates rendered SFT artifacts and must reach the tokenizer artifact used by new training and serving. Existing checkpoint repositories carry their own templates and keep their current behavior.

## Implementation plan

1. In `chat_render.py`, collect analysis text from each assistant turn into `reasoning_content`, leave commentary/final text in `content`, and remove think-token constants and wrapping from the adapter. Join adjacent analysis messages with one newline so their sentences do not run together. Keep tool-call order and the single end-of-turn token.
2. In `MARIN_CHAT_TEMPLATE`, emit one span at the start of every `/think` assistant turn, even when `reasoning_content` is empty; emit none for `/nothink`. Preserve the current nonempty-only rule when the mode is absent or custom. A `/nothink` call with supplied reasoning should omit that reasoning; Datakit normalization only selects `/nothink` when no analysis exists.
3. Bump `CHAT_RENDER_VERSION` to `marin-v4`. Update `docs/tutorials/add-chat-dataset.md` with the new contract and the tokenizer revision. Export and publish a new `marin-community/marin-tokenizer` revision from the same `MARIN_CHAT_TEMPLATE`, then pin that revision for new SFT and serving artifacts that use this format.
4. Rerender the SFT sources used by the target mix in their storage region. Audit every rendered assistant turn by its conversation mode, reporting per-store turn counts, zero-span and multi-span counts under `/think`, spans under `/nothink`, and any interleaved analysis/commentary source records. Require zero format violations before using the stores for training.

## Verification

Extend `tests/test_marin_tokenizer.py` parity cases for an empty `/think` span, two analysis messages, `/nothink`, a call-only turn, and a mixed multi-turn conversation. Compare rendered text and token IDs through the same template used in the exported tokenizer; retain the existing tool-call, assistant-mask, and generation-prompt checks. Run the Datakit rendering tests and repository lint before publishing the tokenizer revision and audit results.

## Open question

For analysis after commentary within one assistant turn, is moving the analysis into the initial span acceptable? The proposed audit will measure whether this occurs before any source-specific repair is chosen.

issues.author: davidlundgren
issues.body:
Part of #10400. Two agent-trajectory sources in the pretraining mixture write reasoning close tags with no opening tag. They are the likely origin of the habit in #10400, where the model closes a think block, keeps reasoning, and closes it again ([scan](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10400#issuecomment-6327348899)).

Counts from one normalized shard per source of `gs://marin-us-central2/datakit/store_8ac06c74`:

- `swe-zero-12m`: 15 of 1,944 documents. In those documents, 197 of 225 assistant turns end their reasoning with `</thinking>` and no opener, and 8 turns close two or more times with reasoning between the closes. A second shard gave 15 of 1,936 documents.
- `davinci-dev/env-native`: 16 of 528 documents have an assistant turn with a bare `</think>`.

These documents are about 0.04% of training tokens, roughly 5M stray close tags over the run. The base checkpoint wrote plain-text `</think>` 6,546 times and `<think>` 307 times in its SWE-bench eval.

The text renderers copy assistant content verbatim: [`swe_zero_12m.row_to_doc`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/swe_zero_12m.py#L98-L107) and [`davinci_dev.env_row_to_doc`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/davinci_dev.py#L224-L234). The `swe-zero-12m` chat conversion wraps all text before the bash block in think tags, `</thinking>` included ([swe_zero_12m.py:156](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/swe_zero_12m.py#L156-L157)), and [`_check_source_markup`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/rollout_transforms.py#L74-L88) matches only `<think>` and `</think>`. [`join_reasoning_and_answer`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/glm_kernelgym_rollouts.py#L74-L82) already repairs the same defect for the GLM kernelgym rollouts.

Done when:
- Rebuilt `swe-zero-12m` and `davinci-dev/env-native` documents have no assistant message with a reasoning close tag that lacks an opener. Pipeline counters report the number of repairs. Tool output and user text are unchanged.
- `swe-zero-12m` chat rows have no `</thinking>` in their reasoning, and `_check_source_markup` also rejects `<thinking>` and `</thinking>`.
- The changed `processed/` and `processed-chat/` steps have new `hash_attrs` versions and are rebuilt.
- The owners of the Hero mixture (`experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/harrier_mix_2026_08_18.py`) have been asked whether its next cooldown uses the rebuilt sources.

🤖

# Research

`swe_zero_12m.row_to_doc` and `davinci_dev.env_row_to_doc` copy assistant content into pretraining text, including unmatched `</thinking>` and `</think>` tags. The SWE-ZERO chat adapter wraps that content in a new think block, and source-markup validation misses `<thinking>` tags. No open PR covers these transforms.

**Relevant code**
- [`swe_zero_12m.py#L98-L107`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/swe_zero_12m.py#L98-L107) — text rendering.

- [`davinci_dev.py#L224-L235`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/davinci_dev.py#L224-L235) — env text rendering.
- [`rollout_transforms.py#L74-L88`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/rollout_transforms.py#L74-L88) — markup check.

# Proposed Fix

Repair unmatched reasoning close tags in assistant content before either text renderer emits a document, and count each repair. Apply the same repair to SWE-ZERO chat reasoning, reject `<thinking>` source markup, and bump the affected `processed/` and `processed-chat/` step versions before rebuilding and checking the outputs. User and tool content stays as recorded.

issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
Track biology evaluation coverage, tooling, and results for reference models and Snowball.

[Biology evaluations catalog](https://openathena.ai/bio-evals/) · [Catalog source](https://github.com/Open-Athena/bio-evals)

**Living summary — updated October 22, 2026.** Detailed evidence is linked from each result.

### Current results

| Model / benchmark | Result | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Snowball v0.1 Smartie Step14 / BixBench corrections v3 / Pi 1.3.0 | **19/205 (9.3%)**; all scored, only 48 nonempty submissions | [Result and reviewed trace audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6300963037) |
| Snowball v0.1 / BiomniBench-DA / Pi 0.87.0 / 60-minute protocol | **4.24/100**; 50/50 scored, 12/50 with any nonempty report (5/50 with both) | [EvalDash](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/20261022-165801-snowball-v01-biomnibench-da-60min-full-b3c4) · [Comparison and audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6349556649) |
| GLM-5.3 / BiomniBench-DA / Pi 0.87.0 / 60-minute protocol | **71.14/100**; 50/50 scored, 45/50 with both reports | [EvalDash](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/20261022-165801-glm-5.3-biomnibench-da-60min-full-b3c4) · [Comparison and audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6349556649) |
| GLM-5.3 / MMLU biology | **462/554**; 81.79% mean subject accuracy, 83.39% pooled | [Run and subject results](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/glm53-mmlu-biology-full-20260918-191647) (Marina access) |
| GLM-5.3 / BixBench CLI v1.5 / Terminus-2 | **101/187 graded (54.01%)**; 18/205 ungraded | [Baseline and limitations](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667) |
| GLM-5.3 / BixBench-Verified-50 / Terminus-2 | **42/49 graded (85.71%)**; 1/50 ungraded; saved-answer regrade | [Regrade and provenance](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/180#issuecomment-5766684283) |
| GLM-5.3 / BixBench-Verified-50 / Pi 0.87.0 | **39/46 graded (84.78%)**; 4/50 ungraded | [Run investigation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6086246928) |

Across benchmark rows, variants, agents, judges, budgets, and grading policies differ. The two BiomniBench-DA rows share the task/input preparation, Pi agent, rubric/judge and budget policy, with disclosed model-serving differences and reused early completions. BiomniBench-DA tasks with no nonempty report score zero; these scores are rubric-score means, not accuracy. Other GLM rows separately report ungraded outcomes.

### Current findings

Snowball’s BixBench failures are dominated by **156 missing answer files**, plus one empty submission. Traces show answers left in chat, simulated execution without real tool calls, repetition, and specific analysis mistakes. Compaction count showed little association with missing files. BFCL also had **55/123 missing submissions**; four inspected examples show related submission/tool-use failures beyond biology, without establishing one shared cause. No scores were changed.

The completed BiomniBench-DA comparison scores **Snowball 4.24/100 versus GLM-5.3 71.14/100**, with all 50 outcomes per model verified against native rewards, sealed archives and EvalDash rows. Snowball produced no nonempty report on 38/50 tasks; GLM did so on 5/50. All 38 selected Snowball cases ended normally within 24 minutes, so the separately confirmed Pi timeout leak cannot explain them. This supports a file-delivery/tool-use gap under these model-serving configurations; checkpoint versus tool/serving integration remains unresolved, and this does not establish a general biology knowledge deficit.

The 60-minute protocol retained 83 unaffected outcomes from the earlier 30-minute budget and reran deadline-affected tasks from scratch. It uses five disclosed input variants and a replacement MiniMax judge/signed rubric scorer, remains supplementary, and does not change the release aggregate. The continuation used the [Harbor timeout repair](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/commit/3bc27cbcffad1d92ad5d9bd4c83cd3f36bf89372); an unresolved `/tokenize` HTTP 502 diagnostic affects interpretation of one GLM timeout. [Full comparison, launch-source references, audit and limitations](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6349556649).

[Selected HF traces](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples) show recurring simulated execution, chat-only answers, and repetitive output-limit failures across BiomniBench-DA, BixBench, and BFCL. BiomniBench also has wrong-path and rejected-write examples. These support general execution/submission problems without establishing a shared cause; [the comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6297505720) records the examples and differing Pi versions.

comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 The five-question GLM-5.3 BixBench CLI pilot completed with an answer from every task. The original verifier scored three answers: one correct, two incorrect, and two unscored because structured JSON generation exhausted the judge's token limit. The incomplete original run retains no aggregate metric.

A separate, uniform regrade of the same five saved answers added an explicit JSON-schema instruction to the judge. It produced one correct and four incorrect results, with no JSON errors; the three previously valid grades stayed unchanged. This is a five-question integration pilot with a disclosed judge-prompt variation, not a full-benchmark accuracy estimate. The original answers, trajectories, and scores were preserved.

The format repair is in [Harbor commit `97037f79`](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/commit/97037f793efaae22e22da5b89bc9604d2e40e800). It preserves the comparison prompt, Boolean schema, judge model, and 1,024-token cap. Lint and formatting passed. The branch has no PR yet; existing registry snapshots still require regenerated or explicitly patched tasks.

Error review:

- `bix-11-q2`: 88/249 fungal trees exceed the treeness threshold, giving 35.34%, versus the reference's 35%. The regrader rejected the difference. This is a likely precision-related false negative; no score has been changed. The pinned question specifies no rounding rule, and its archive contains no reference notebook.
- `bix-52-q2`: the agent used pooled CpGs / genome length. The [reference capsule](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-4dceea58-7d66-4576-bfc6-88c026d5b7a9.zip) groups only chromosomes containing retained CpGs (notebook cells 11 and 39). Averaging those 20 chromosome densities yields 1.1283e-7, inside the reference interval. The notebook confirms the chromosome selection; the mean was recomputed from the saved table.
- `bix-28-q1`: the final analysis substituted raw terminal branch lengths and species-level medians for the [PhyKIT long-branch statistic](https://jlsteenwyk.com/PhyKIT/reference/commands/long_branch_score.html). The reference p-value has not been independently reproduced; its archive also contains no reference notebook.
- `bix-6-q7`: the agent used a top-1% replicate intersection, then mistook its own intermediate enrichment CSV for supplied results. The [reference notebook](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-f4dcda89-678d-403d-b155-1483d0071765.zip), cells 28–30, instead takes the minimum replicate P-value, selects values below 0.05, maps RefSeq IDs to symbols, and runs Reactome enrichment against measured genes. It reports “cGMP effects” with raw P ≈ 0.000024 and adjusted P ≈ 0.0327. These are saved reference outputs, not a fresh rerun.
- `bix-18-q2`: the mean swarming area was correctly rounded to 82,000.

Six additional fixed judge diagnostics accepted `35.0%` as equivalent to `35%`, rejected `45%`, and classified one value inside and one outside the CpG reference interval correctly. The exact-percent and higher-precision examples returned provider server errors, so this check did not resolve the rounding concern. No tolerance or solver setting was retuned.

The [previously documented protocol](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5736346928) and explicit environment overrides were retained. All five pilot agents submitted within their original time limits, with no observed disk exhaustion. The full 205-question run remains pending a decision on numerical grading; original scores will remain intact.

comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 GLM-5.3 completed 205 fresh BixBench CLI attempts: **101 correct / 187 graded (54.01%)**, with **18 ungraded**. Grading coverage is **91.22%**. Marin's 95% interval accounting for ungraded items is **43.79–63.43%**; 54.01% is the accuracy among graded questions.
